verses.1:1: There was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from Mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.
verses.1:2: And he had two wives; the name of one was Hannah, and the name of the second was Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
verses.1:3: And that man used to go up from his city on the appointed days to worship and sacrifice to the Lord of hosts in Shiloh. Now the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, priests of the Lord, were there.
verses.1:4: So the day came, and Elkanah offered sacrifice, and he gave portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
verses.1:5: But to Hannah he gave one portion sorrowfully, because he loved Hannah. However, the Lord had closed her womb.
verses.1:6: Her rival also afflicted her and distressed her severely, to such an extent that she reproached her because the Lord had closed her womb.
verses.1:7: And so she did every single year: when, as the time returned, they went up to the temple of the Lord, so she provoked her; meanwhile she wept and would not take food.
verses.1:8: So her husband Elkanah said to her, "Hannah, why are you weeping? And why are you not eating? And for what reason is your heart afflicted? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
verses.1:9: Now Hannah rose after she had eaten and drunk in Shiloh. And while Eli the priest was sitting on a seat before the doorposts of the temple of the Lord,
verses.1:10: Hannah, being bitter in spirit, prayed to the Lord, weeping profusely,
verses.1:11: and she vowed a vow, saying, "Lord of hosts, if looking on You see the affliction of Your female servant, and remember me, and do not forget Your maidservant, and give Your servant a male child, I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life, and no razor will come upon his head."
verses.1:12: Now it happened, while she was multiplying prayers before the Lord, that Eli watched her mouth.
verses.1:13: Now Hannah was speaking in her heart, and only her lips were moving, and no voice at all was heard. Therefore Eli considered her to be drunk,
verses.1:14: and he said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Work off for a little while the wine with which you are drenched."
verses.1:15: Answering, Hannah said, "By no means, my lord, for I am an exceedingly unhappy woman; and I have not drunk wine or anything that can intoxicate, but I have poured out my soul in the sight of the Lord.
verses.1:16: Do not reckon your maidservant as one of the daughters of Belial, for out of the abundance of my grief and sorrow I have spoken up to the present."
verses.1:17: Then Eli said to her, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you your petition that you have asked of Him."
verses.1:18: And she said, "May your maidservant find favor in your eyes." And the woman went on her way and ate, and her countenance was no longer changed in different ways.
verses.1:19: And they rose in the morning and worshiped before the Lord; and they returned and came to their house in Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her.
verses.1:20: And it happened after the cycle of days that Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, because she had asked for him from the Lord.
verses.1:21: Now her husband Elkanah went up, and all his household, to offer to the Lord the solemn sacrifice and his vow.
verses.1:22: And Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "I will not go until the infant is weaned, and I will bring him so that he may appear before the sight of the Lord and remain there continually."
verses.1:23: And her husband Elkanah said to her, "Do what seems good to you, and remain until you wean him; and I pray that the Lord may fulfill His word." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she took him off milk.
verses.1:24: And she brought him with her after she had weaned him, with three calves, and three measures of flour, and a jar of wine, and she brought him to the house of the Lord in Shiloh. Now the boy was still a very small child;
verses.1:25: and they sacrificed a calf, and they presented the boy to Eli.
verses.1:26: And Hannah said, "I beg you, my lord, as your soul lives, my lord, I am that woman who stood before you here, praying to the Lord.
verses.1:27: For this boy I prayed, and the Lord has given me my petition that I asked of Him.
verses.1:28: Therefore I also have lent him to the Lord for all the days in which he is lent to the Lord." And they worshiped the Lord there. And Hannah prayed and said:
verses.2:1: "My heart has exulted in the Lord, and my horn has been exalted in my God; my mouth has opened wide over my enemies, because I have rejoiced in Your salvation.
verses.2:2: There is no one holy as the Lord is, for indeed there is no other besides You, and there is no strong one like our God.
verses.2:3: Do not multiply speaking lofty things while boasting; let old things depart from your mouth, for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and for Him thoughts are prepared.
verses.2:4: The bow of the mighty has been overcome, and the weak have been girded with strength.
verses.2:5: Those who were full before have hired themselves out for bread, and the hungry have been satisfied, until the barren woman has borne very many, and she who had many children has been weakened.
verses.2:6: The Lord puts to death and makes alive; He brings down to the underworld and brings back up.
verses.2:7: The Lord makes poor and enriches; He humbles and lifts up.
verses.2:8: He raises up the needy from the dust and lifts up the poor from the dung, so that he may sit with princes and hold a throne of glory. For the pivots of the earth belong to the Lord, and He has set the world upon them.
verses.2:9: He will guard the feet of His holy ones, and the wicked will fall silent in darkness, for not by his own strength will a man be made strong.
verses.2:10: His adversaries will dread the Lord, and over them He will thunder in the heavens. The Lord will judge the ends of the earth, and He will give dominion to His king, and He will lift high the horn of His anointed one."
verses.2:11: And Elkanah went away to Ramah, to his house; but the boy was a minister in the sight of the Lord before the face of Eli the priest.
verses.2:12: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial, not knowing the Lord,
verses.2:13: nor the duty of the priests toward the people; rather, whenever anyone had offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was being cooked, and he had a three-pronged fork in his hand,
verses.2:14: and he would thrust it into the kettle, or into the cauldron, or into the pot, or into the pan; and everything that the fork lifted up, the priest took for himself. Thus they did to all Israel who came to Shiloh.
verses.2:15: Even before they burned the fat, the priest's servant would come and say to the one offering sacrifice, "Give me meat to cook for the priest, for I will not accept cooked meat from you, but raw."
verses.2:16: And the one offering sacrifice would say to him, "Let the fat be burned first today according to custom, and take for yourself as much as your soul desires." And answering, he would say to him, "By no means; for you will give it now, otherwise I will take it by force."
verses.2:17: Therefore the sin of the young men was exceedingly great before the Lord, because they were holding people back from the sacrifice of the Lord.
verses.2:18: Now Samuel was ministering before the face of the Lord, a boy girded with a linen ephod.
verses.2:19: And his mother used to make a small tunic for him, which she would bring on the appointed days when going up with her husband to offer the solemn sacrifice.
verses.2:20: And Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and he said to him, "May the Lord repay you with offspring from this woman for the loan that you have lent to the Lord." And they went away to their own place.
verses.2:21: Therefore the Lord visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel was magnified before the Lord.
verses.2:22: Now Eli was very old, and he heard everything that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they were sleeping with the women who kept watch at the doorway of the tabernacle;
verses.2:23: and he said to them, "Why do you do things of this kind, most wicked things, which I hear from all the people?
verses.2:24: No, my sons, for it is not a good report that I hear, that you are making the people of the Lord transgress.
verses.2:25: If a man sins against a man, God can be appeased for him; but if a man sins against the Lord, who will pray for him?" And they did not listen to the voice of their father, because the Lord willed to kill them.
verses.2:26: Now the boy Samuel was advancing and growing, and he was pleasing both to the Lord and to people.
verses.2:27: Now a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the Lord says: Was I not openly revealed to the house of your father, when they were in Egypt in the house of Pharaoh?
verses.2:28: And I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel for Myself as a priest, so that he might go up to My altar, and burn incense to Me, and bear an ephod before Me; and I gave to the house of your father everything from the sacrifices of the sons of Israel.
verses.2:29: Why have you kicked away My sacrifice and My offerings that I commanded to be offered in the temple, and honored your sons more than Me, so that you might eat the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel, My people?
verses.2:30: Therefore the Lord God of Israel says: I certainly spoke that your house and the house of your father should minister in My sight forever. But now the Lord says: Far be this from Me; rather, whoever glorifies Me, I will glorify him, but those who despise Me will be without honor.
verses.2:31: Look, the days are coming, and I will cut off your arm and the arm of the house of your father, so that there will not be an old man in your house.
verses.2:32: And you will see your rival in the temple, in all the prosperity of Israel; and there will not be an old man in your house for all days.
verses.2:33: Nevertheless, I will not completely take away a man of yours from My altar, but so that your eyes may fail and your soul may waste away; and a great part of your house will die when they reach manhood.
verses.2:34: And this will be a sign to you, what is about to come upon your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: on one day both of them will die.
verses.2:35: And I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest, who will act according to My heart and My soul; and I will build for him a faithful house, and he will walk before My anointed one for all days.
verses.2:36: And it will come about that whoever remains in your house will come so that prayer may be made for him, and will offer a silver coin and a loaf of bread, and will say, 'Admit me, I beg you, to one priestly office, so that I may eat a morsel of bread.'"
verses.3:1: Now the boy Samuel was ministering to the Lord before Eli, and the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no clear vision.
verses.3:2: So it happened on a certain day that Eli was lying in his place, and his eyes had grown dim, nor could he see.
verses.3:3: Before the lamp of God was extinguished, Samuel was sleeping in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was.
verses.3:4: And the Lord called Samuel. Answering, he said, "Here I am."
verses.3:5: And he ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." And he said, "I did not call; return and sleep." And he went away and slept.
verses.3:6: And the Lord proceeded again to call Samuel. And rising up, Samuel went to Eli and said, "Here I am, because you called me." And he answered, "I did not call you, my son; return and sleep."
verses.3:7: Moreover, Samuel did not yet know the Lord, nor had the word of the Lord been revealed to him.
verses.3:8: And the Lord continued and called Samuel yet a third time. And rising up, he went to Eli,
verses.3:9: and said, "Here I am, because you called me." Then Eli understood that the Lord was calling the boy, and he said to Samuel, "Go and sleep; and if He calls you after this, you will say, 'Speak, Lord, because Your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went away and slept in his place.
verses.3:10: And the Lord came and stood, and called, just as He had called the second time, "Samuel, Samuel." And Samuel said, "Speak, Lord, because Your servant is listening."
verses.3:11: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Look, I am doing a thing in Israel; for whoever hears it, both of his ears will tingle.
verses.3:12: On that day I will raise up against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house; I will begin, and I will finish.
verses.3:13: For I foretold to him that I would judge his house forever because of the iniquity, since he knew that his sons were acting unworthily, and he did not rebuke them.
verses.3:14: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of his house will not be expiated by sacrifices and offerings for all eternity."
verses.3:15: Now Samuel slept until morning, and he opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel was afraid to report the vision to Eli.
verses.3:16: Then Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son?" Answering, he said, "I am here."
verses.3:17: And he asked him, "What is the word that the Lord spoke to you? I beg you, do not hide it from me; may God do these things to you, and add these as well, if you conceal from me a word from all the words that were spoken to you."
verses.3:18: Therefore Samuel reported all the words to him, and did not conceal them from him. And he answered, "He is the Lord; let Him do what is good in His eyes."
verses.3:19: Now Samuel grew, and the Lord was with him, and none of all his words fell to the ground.
verses.3:20: And all Israel, from Dan as far as Beersheba, knew that Samuel was a faithful prophet of the Lord.
verses.3:21: And the Lord continued to appear in Shiloh, since the Lord had been revealed to Samuel in Shiloh according to the word of the Lord. And the word of Samuel came to all Israel.
verses.4:1: And it happened in those days that the Philistines assembled for combat; and Israel went out to meet the Philistines for battle, and encamped beside the Stone of Help. Meanwhile, the Philistines came to Aphek,
verses.4:2: and drew up the battle line against Israel. Now when the engagement had begun, Israel turned its back to the Philistines; and about four thousand men were cut down in that engagement here and there throughout the fields.
verses.4:3: And the people returned to the camp, and the elders of Israel said, "Why has the Lord struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord to us from Shiloh, and let it come into our midst, so that it may save us from the hand of our enemies."
verses.4:4: Therefore the people sent to Shiloh, and from there they brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts, who sits upon the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli were with the ark of the covenant of God, Hophni and Phinehas.
verses.4:5: And when the ark of the covenant of the Lord had come into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, and the earth resounded.
verses.4:6: And the Philistines heard the sound of the shout, and they said, "What is this sound of a great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of the Lord had come into the camp.
verses.4:7: And the Philistines were afraid, saying, "God has come into the camp." And they groaned, saying,
verses.4:8: "Woe to us! For there was not such great exultation yesterday and the day before; woe to us! Who will save us from the hand of these exalted gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every plague in the desert.
verses.4:9: Be strong and be men, Philistines, so that you do not serve the Hebrews, just as they also served you; be strong and fight."
verses.4:10: So the Philistines fought, and Israel was cut down, and each one fled to his tent; and an exceedingly great slaughter took place, and thirty thousand foot soldiers fell from Israel.
verses.4:11: And the ark of God was captured; the two sons of Eli also died, Hophni and Phinehas.
verses.4:12: Now a man of Benjamin, running from the battle line, came to Shiloh on that day, with his garment torn and his head sprinkled with dust.
verses.4:13: And when he had arrived, Eli was sitting upon a seat, looking toward the road. For his heart was trembling for the ark of God. Now after that man had entered, he reported it to the city, and the entire city wailed.
verses.4:14: And Eli heard the sound of the outcry, and he said, "What is this sound of this tumult?" And that man hurried, and came, and reported to Eli.
verses.4:15: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes had grown dim, and he could not see.
verses.4:16: And he said to Eli, "I am the one who came from the battle, and I am the one who fled from the battle line today." And he said to him, "What has happened, my son?"
verses.4:17: Now the one who was reporting answered, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and a great ruin has occurred among the people; furthermore, your two sons also have died, Hophni and Phinehas, and the ark of God has been captured."
verses.4:18: And when he had mentioned the ark of God, he fell backward from the seat beside the door, and with his neck broken, he died. For the man was old and advanced in age; and he himself judged Israel for forty years.
verses.4:19: Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and near to childbirth; and upon hearing the report that the ark of God had been captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she bowed herself down and gave birth, for sudden pains had rushed upon her.
verses.4:20: Now at the very moment of her death, the women who were standing around her said to her, "Do not be afraid, because you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer them, nor did she pay attention.
verses.4:21: And she called the boy Ichabod, saying, "The glory has been carried away from Israel," because the ark of God was captured, and on account of her father-in-law and her husband;
verses.4:22: and she said, "The glory has been carried away from Israel, because the ark of God was captured."
verses.5:1: Now the Philistines took the ark of God, and carried it away from the Stone of Help to Ashdod.
verses.5:2: And the Philistines took the ark of God, and brought it into the temple of Dagon, and set it beside Dagon.
verses.5:3: And when the Ashdodites had risen at dawn on the next day, look, Dagon was lying prone on the ground before the ark of the Lord; and they took Dagon and restored him to his place.
verses.5:4: And rising up again in the morning on the next day, they found Dagon lying upon his face on the ground before the ark of the Lord; now the head of Dagon and the two palms of his hands had been cut off upon the threshold.
verses.5:5: Meanwhile, only the trunk of Dagon had remained in its place. For this reason the priests of Dagon, and all who enter his temple, do not step upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to the present day.
verses.5:6: Now the hand of the Lord weighed heavily upon the Ashdodites, and He devastated them, and He struck Ashdod and its borders in the more hidden part of the buttocks. And the villages and fields in the middle of that region teemed, and mice sprang up, and a confusion of great death occurred in the city.
verses.5:7: Now the men of Ashdod, seeing this kind of plague, said, "Let the ark of the God of Israel not remain with us, because His hand is harsh upon us, and upon Dagon our god."
verses.5:8: And sending out, they gathered all the satraps of the Philistines to themselves, and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" And the Gittites answered, "Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried around." And they carried the ark of the God of Israel around.
verses.5:9: Now while they were carrying it around, the hand of the Lord throughout each city became one of exceedingly great slaughter, and it struck the men of every city, from the small to the great, and their protruding lower bowels were rotting. And the Gittites took counsel and made for themselves leather seats.
verses.5:10: Therefore they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And when the ark of God had come into Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, "They have brought the ark of the God of Israel to us so that it may kill us and our people."
verses.5:11: Therefore they sent and gathered all the satraps of the Philistines, who said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its own place, and let it not kill us with our people."
verses.5:12: For a terror of death was arising in each city, and the hand of God was very heavy indeed. The men also who had not died were being struck in the more hidden part of the buttocks, and the wailing of every city went up to heaven.
verses.6:1: So the ark of the Lord was in the region of the Philistines for seven months.
verses.6:2: And the Philistines called the priests and diviners, saying, "What will we do with the ark of the Lord? Show us how we should send it back to its own place." And they said,
verses.6:3: "If you send back the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but render to Him what you owe for sin; and then you will be healed, and you will know why His hand does not withdraw from you."
verses.6:4: And they said, "What is it that we ought to render to Him for the trespass?" And they answered,
verses.6:5: "According to the number of the provinces of the Philistines, you will make five golden anuses and five golden mice, because one plague was upon all of you and upon your satraps. And you will make likenesses of your anuses and likenesses of the mice that have devastated the land, and you will give glory to the God of Israel, if perhaps He may lift His hand from you, and from your gods, and from your land.
verses.6:6: Why do you harden your hearts, just as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? After he was struck, did he not then let them go, and they departed?
verses.6:7: Now therefore, take and make one new cart, and hitch to the cart two cows with calves on which no yoke has been placed, and shut up their calves at home.
verses.6:8: And you will take the ark of the Lord and place it on the cart, and the golden articles that you have paid to Him for the trespass you will place in a small box at its side, and send it away so that it may go.
verses.6:9: And you will watch, and if indeed it goes up by the way of its own borders toward Beth-shemesh, He Himself has done this great evil to us; but if not, then not at all: we will know that His hand by no means touched us, but it happened by chance."
verses.6:10: So they did in this manner, and taking two cows that were nursing calves, they hitched them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.
verses.6:11: And they placed the ark of God upon the cart, and the small box that held the golden mice and the likenesses of the anuses.
verses.6:12: Now the cows went straight along the way that leads to Beth-shemesh, and they walked along one path, proceeding and lowing, and they did not turn aside either to the right or to the left; and indeed the satraps of the Philistines were following as far as the borders of Beth-shemesh.
verses.6:13: Now the Beth-shemites were harvesting wheat in the valley, and lifting up their eyes, they saw the ark and rejoiced when they saw it.
verses.6:14: And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite and stood still there. Now a large stone was there; and they chopped up the timbers of the cart and placed the cows upon them as a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.6:15: And the Levites took down the ark of God and the small box that was beside it, in which were the golden articles, and placed them upon the great stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed victims to the Lord on that day.
verses.6:16: And the five satraps of the Philistines saw it, and returned to Ekron on that day.
verses.6:17: Now these are the golden anuses that the Philistines rendered to the Lord for the trespass: Ashdod one, Gaza one, Ashkelon one, Gath one, Ekron one;
verses.6:18: and the golden mice according to the number of the cities of the Philistines of the five provinces, from the walled city to the village that was without a wall, and as far as Great Abel, upon which they placed the ark of the Lord, which was until that day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite.
verses.6:19: And He struck some of the men of Beth-shemesh because they had seen the ark of the Lord; and He struck from the people seventy men and fifty thousand of the common people. And the people mourned because the Lord had struck the common people with a great plague.
verses.6:20: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who will be able to stand in the sight of this holy Lord God? And to whom will He go up from us?"
verses.6:21: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The Philistines have brought back the ark of the Lord; come down and bring it back to yourselves."
verses.7:1: So the men of Kiriath-jearim came and brought back the ark of the Lord, and brought it into the house of Abinadab in Gibeah; and they sanctified Eleazar his son to guard the ark of the Lord.
verses.7:2: And it happened that from the day on which the ark of the Lord remained in Kiriath-jearim, the days were multiplied (for it was already the twentieth year), and all the house of Israel rested after the Lord.
verses.7:3: And Samuel spoke to the entire house of Israel, saying, "If you are returning to the Lord with your whole heart, remove the foreign gods from your midst, the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and prepare your hearts for the Lord, and serve Him alone, and He will rescue you from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:4: So the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the Lord alone.
verses.7:5: And Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, so that I may pray to the Lord for you."
verses.7:6: And they assembled at Mizpah, and drew water and poured it out in the sight of the Lord; and they fasted on that day and said there, "We have sinned against the Lord." And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.
verses.7:7: And the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had been gathered together at Mizpah, and the satraps of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the sons of Israel heard this, they were afraid before the Philistines.
verses.7:8: And they said to Samuel, "Do not cease crying out for us to the Lord our God, so that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.7:9: And Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the Lord; and Samuel cried out to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.
verses.7:10: Now it happened, while Samuel was offering the burnt offering, that the Philistines entered into battle against Israel; but the Lord thundered with a great crash on that day over the Philistines and terrified them, and they were struck down before Israel.
verses.7:11: And the men of Israel went out from Mizpah, pursued the Philistines, and struck them as far as the place that was below Beth-car.
verses.7:12: Then Samuel took one stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and he called the name of that place Stone of Help. And he said, "Up to this point the Lord has helped us."
verses.7:13: And the Philistines were humbled, and they did not come again into the borders of Israel. And so the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
verses.7:14: And the cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and their borders; and He delivered Israel from the hand of the Philistines, and there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.7:15: Samuel also judged Israel all the days of his life;
verses.7:16: and he went year by year making a circuit of Bethel and Gilgal and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in the aforementioned places.
verses.7:17: And he would return to Ramah, for his house was there, and there he judged Israel; he also built an altar there to the Lord.
verses.8:1: Now it happened, when Samuel had grown old, that he appointed his sons as judges of Israel.
verses.8:2: And the name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of the second was Abijah, judges in Beersheba.
verses.8:3: And his sons did not walk in his ways, but turned aside after greed, and accepted bribes, and perverted justice.
verses.8:4: Therefore all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.
verses.8:5: And they said to him, "Look, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways; appoint a king for us to judge us, just as all the nations also have."
verses.8:6: The word was displeasing in the eyes of Samuel because they had said, "Give us a king to judge us." And Samuel prayed to the Lord.
verses.8:7: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in everything that they say to you, for they have not rejected you, but Me, so that I should not reign over them.
verses.8:8: According to all their deeds that they have done from the day on which I brought them out of Egypt until this day: just as they have abandoned Me and served foreign gods, so they are also doing to you.
verses.8:9: Now therefore, listen to their voice; yet solemnly warn them and foretell to them the right of the king who is going to reign over them."
verses.8:10: And so Samuel spoke all the words of the Lord to the people who had asked a king from him.
verses.8:11: And he said, "This will be the right of the king who is going to rule over you: he will take your sons and place them in his chariots, and he will make them horsemen for himself and forerunners of his four-horse chariots,
verses.8:12: and he will appoint for himself tribunes and centurions, and plowmen of his fields, and reapers of the crops, and craftsmen of his weapons and of his chariots.
verses.8:13: He will also make your daughters perfumers, cooks, and bakers for himself.
verses.8:14: He will also take your fields, and vineyards, and best olive groves, and give them to his servants.
verses.8:15: Moreover, he will take a tenth of your crops and of the yield of your vineyards, so that he may give it to his eunuchs and his attendants.
verses.8:16: He will also take away your male servants and female servants, and your best young men, and your donkeys, and put them to his own work.
verses.8:17: He will also take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will be servants to him.
verses.8:18: And you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, and the Lord will not hear you on that day, because you have asked a king for yourselves."
verses.8:19: However, the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, but they said, "By no means, for there will be a king over us,
verses.8:20: and we also will be like all the nations, and our king will judge us and go out before us and fight our battles for us."
verses.8:21: And Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he spoke them in the ears of the Lord.
verses.8:22: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Listen to their voice, and appoint a king over them." And Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Let each one go to his own city."
verses.9:1: And there was a man of Benjamin named Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a man of Jemini, mighty in strength.
verses.9:2: And he had a son called Saul, choice and good, and there was no man among the sons of Israel better than he; from the shoulder and upward he towered above all the people.
verses.9:3: Now the female donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, had been lost; and Kish said to his son Saul, "Take one of the servants with you, and get up, go, and search for the female donkeys." And when they had passed through Mount Ephraim,
verses.9:4: and through the land of Shalishah, and had not found them, they passed also through the land of Shaalim, and they were not there; and also through the land of Jemini, and they did not find them at all.
verses.9:5: Now when they had come into the land of Zuph, Saul said to the servant who was with him, "Come and let us return, for fear that my father may have given up the female donkeys and be anxious about us."
verses.9:6: And he said to him, "Look, there is a man of God in this city, a distinguished man; everything that he speaks comes about without uncertainty. Now therefore let us go there, in case perhaps he may tell us about our way, on account of which we have come."
verses.9:7: And Saul said to his servant, "Look, we will go; what shall we bring to the man of God? The bread has run out in our provision bags, and we have no gift to give to the man of God, nor anything else."
verses.9:8: Again the servant answered Saul and said, "Look, a fourth part of a stater of silver is found in my hand; let us give it to the man of God, so that he may show us our way."
verses.9:9: (Formerly in Israel, everyone going to consult God used to speak like this: "Come, and let us go to the seer." For the one who is called a prophet today was formerly called a seer.)
verses.9:10: And Saul said to his servant, "Your word is very good. Come, let us go." And they went to the city in which the man of God was.
verses.9:11: And as they were going up the slope of the city, they found young women coming out to draw water, and they said to them, "Is the seer here?"
verses.9:12: And answering, they said to them, "He is here; look, he is ahead of you. Hurry now, for today he has come into the city, because there is a sacrifice of the people today at the high place.
verses.9:13: As you enter the city, you will immediately find him before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he himself blesses the sacrifice, and afterward those who are invited eat. Now therefore go up, because today you will find him."
verses.9:14: And they went up into the city. And as they were walking in the middle of the city, Samuel appeared, coming out to meet them in order to go up to the high place.
verses.9:15: Now the Lord had uncovered Samuel's ear one day before Saul came, saying,
verses.9:16: "At this very hour that it is now, tomorrow I will send a man to you from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as leader over My people Israel; and he will save My people from the hand of the Philistines, because I have looked upon My people, for their cry has come to Me."
verses.9:17: And when Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said to him, "Here is the man of whom I had spoken to you; this one will rule over My people."
verses.9:18: Now Saul approached Samuel in the middle of the gate and said, "Tell me, please, where the house of the seer is."
verses.9:19: And Samuel answered Saul, saying, "I am the seer. Go up ahead of me to the high place, so that you may eat with me today, and I will send you away in the morning, and I will tell you all that is in your heart.
verses.9:20: And concerning the female donkeys that you lost three days ago, do not be anxious, because they have been found. And whose will all the best things of Israel be? Will they not belong to you and to all the house of your father?"
verses.9:21: Now Saul answered and said, "Am I not a son of Jemini, from the smallest tribe of Israel, and is not my clan the least among all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken this word to me?"
verses.9:22: Therefore Samuel, taking Saul and his servant, brought them into the dining hall and gave them a place at the head of those who had been invited; for there were about thirty men.
verses.9:23: And Samuel said to the cook, "Give the portion that I gave to you and commanded you to set aside by yourself."
verses.9:24: Now the cook lifted up the shoulder and set it before Saul. And Samuel said, "Look, what has remained: set it before you and eat, because it was intentionally kept for you when I invited the people." And Saul ate with Samuel on that day.
verses.9:25: And they came down from the high place into the town, and he spoke with Saul on the rooftop; and Saul spread a bed on the rooftop and slept.
verses.9:26: And when they had risen in the morning, and it was already growing light, Samuel called Saul on the rooftop, saying, "Get up, and I will send you away." And Saul got up; and both of them went out, namely he himself and Samuel.
verses.9:27: And as they were going down at the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the servant to go ahead of us and pass on; but you stand still for a little while, so that I may tell you the word of the Lord."
verses.10:1: Now Samuel took a flask of oil and poured it upon his head, and kissed him and said, "Look, the Lord has anointed you over His inheritance as prince, and you will deliver His people from the hands of their enemies who are all around them. And this shall be a sign to you that God has anointed you as prince.
verses.10:2: When you depart from me today, you will find two men beside the tomb of Rachel in the territory of Benjamin, in the south; and they will say to you, 'The female donkeys that you had gone to search for have been found; and your father, having put aside the female donkeys, is anxious about you and says, "What shall I do about my son?"'
verses.10:3: And when you depart from there, and pass farther on, and come to the oak of Tabor, three men going up to God at Bethel will find you there, one carrying three young goats, and another three loaves of bread, and another carrying a jar of wine.
verses.10:4: And when they have greeted you, they will give you two loaves of bread, and you shall accept them from their hand.
verses.10:5: After these things you will come to the hill of God, where the garrison of the Philistines is; and when you have entered the city there, you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place, and before them a harp, a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre, and they themselves prophesying.
verses.10:6: And the Spirit of the Lord will leap upon you, and you will prophesy with them, and you will be changed into another man.
verses.10:7: When therefore all these signs have come about for you, do whatever your hand finds, because the Lord is with you.
verses.10:8: And you shall go down ahead of me to Gilgal (for I indeed will come down to you), so that you may offer an offering and sacrifice peace offerings; for seven days you shall wait until I come to you and show you what you are to do."
verses.10:9: And so, when he had turned his shoulder to depart from Samuel, God changed his heart into another, and all these signs came about on that day.
verses.10:10: And they came to the aforementioned hill, and look, a company of prophets met him; and the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon him, and he prophesied in the midst of them.
verses.10:11: Now all who had known him yesterday and the day before, seeing that he was with the prophets and was prophesying, said to one another, "What thing has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:12: And one answered another, saying, "And who is their father?" Therefore it turned into a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.10:13: Now he stopped prophesying and came to the high place.
verses.10:14: And Saul's uncle said to him and to his servant, "Where did you go?" And they answered, "To search for the female donkeys; and when we had not found them, we came to Samuel."
verses.10:15: And his uncle said to him, "Tell me what Samuel said to you."
verses.10:16: And Saul said to his uncle, "He told us that the female donkeys had been found." But concerning the word of the kingdom that Samuel had spoken to him, he did not tell him.
verses.10:17: And Samuel summoned the people to the Lord at Mizpah,
verses.10:18: and he said to the sons of Israel, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says: 'I brought Israel out of Egypt, and rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all the kings who were afflicting you.'
verses.10:19: But today you have rejected your God, who alone has saved you from all your evils and tribulations; and you have said, 'By no means, but set a king over us.' Now therefore stand before the Lord by your tribes and by your families."
verses.10:20: And Samuel brought forward all the tribes of Israel, and the lot of the tribe of Benjamin fell.
verses.10:21: And he brought forward the tribe of Benjamin and its clans, and the clan of Matri fell; and it came down to Saul the son of Kish. Therefore they searched for him, and he was not found.
verses.10:22: And after these things they consulted the Lord as to whether he would come there. And the Lord answered, "Look, he is hidden at home."
verses.10:23: Therefore they ran and brought him from there; and he stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than all the people from the shoulder and upward.
verses.10:24: And Samuel said to all the people, "Surely you see the one whom the Lord has chosen, that there is no one like him among all the people." And all the people shouted and said, "May the king live!"
verses.10:25: Now Samuel spoke to the people the law of the kingdom, and wrote it in a book, and deposited it before the Lord; and Samuel sent all the people away, each one to his own house.
verses.10:26: And Saul also went away to his house in Gibeah; and there went with him a part of the army, whose hearts God had touched.
verses.10:27: But the sons of Belial said, "Will this one be able to save us?" And they despised him and did not bring him gifts; but he pretended not to hear.
verses.11:1: And it happened about a month later that Nahash the Ammonite went up and began to fight against Jabesh-gilead. And all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Have us as allies, and we will serve you."
verses.11:2: And Nahash the Ammonite answered them, "On this condition I will make a treaty with you: that I gouge out the right eyes of all of you, and make you a reproach in all Israel."
verses.11:3: And the elders of Jabesh said to him, "Grant us seven days, so that we may send messengers to all the territories of Israel; and if there is no one to defend us, we will come out to you."
verses.11:4: Therefore the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke these words in the hearing of the people; and all the people lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.11:5: And look, Saul was coming, following the oxen from the field, and he said, "What is wrong with the people, that they are weeping?" And they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
verses.11:6: And the Spirit of the Lord leaped upon Saul when he had heard these words, and his anger grew exceedingly fierce.
verses.11:7: And taking both oxen, he cut them into pieces and sent them into all the territories of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, "Whoever does not come out and follow Saul and Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen." Therefore the fear of the Lord seized the people, and they went out as one man.
verses.11:8: And he mustered them at Bezek; and of the sons of Israel there were three hundred thousand, and of the men of Judah thirty thousand.
verses.11:9: And they said to the messengers who had come, "Thus you shall say to the men who are in Jabesh-gilead: 'Tomorrow there will be deliverance for you, when the sun grows hot.'" Therefore the messengers came and reported to the men of Jabesh, who rejoiced.
verses.11:10: And they said, "In the morning we will come out to you, and you may do to us everything that pleases you."
verses.11:11: And it happened, when the next day had come, that Saul arranged the people into three divisions; and he entered the middle of the camp in the morning watch and struck Ammon until the day grew hot; and the rest were scattered, so that not two among them were left together.
verses.11:12: And the people said to Samuel, "Who is this one who said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Hand over the men, and we will put them to death."
verses.11:13: And Saul said, "No one shall be put to death on this day, because today the Lord has accomplished deliverance in Israel."
verses.11:14: Now Samuel said to the people, "Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and let us renew the kingdom there."
verses.11:15: And all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal, and there they sacrificed peace offerings before the Lord. And there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced exceedingly.
verses.12:1: Now Samuel said to all Israel, "Look, I have listened to your voice in accordance with everything that you have spoken to me, and I have appointed a king over you.
verses.12:2: And now the king walks before you, while I have grown old and turned gray; moreover, my sons are with you. And so, having lived before you from my youth until this day, look, I stand ready.
verses.12:3: Speak concerning me before the Lord and before His anointed, whether I have taken anyone's ox or donkey, if I have falsely accused anyone, if I have oppressed anyone, if I have accepted a gift from anyone's hand; and I will despise it today, and restore it to you."
verses.12:4: And they said, "You have not falsely accused us, nor oppressed us, nor taken anything from anyone's hand."
verses.12:5: And he said to them, "The Lord is a witness against you, and His anointed is a witness on this day, that you have not found anything in my hand." And they said, "He is a witness."
verses.12:6: And Samuel said to the people, "It is the Lord, who made Moses and Aaron, and brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt.
verses.12:7: Now therefore, stand, so that I may contend in judgment against you before the Lord concerning all the mercies of the Lord that He performed for you and for your fathers:
verses.12:8: how Jacob entered Egypt, and your fathers cried out to the Lord, and the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, and brought your fathers out of Egypt, and settled them in this place.
verses.12:9: Yet they forgot the Lord their God, and He handed them over into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.
verses.12:10: Afterward, however, they cried out to the Lord and said, 'We have sinned, because we have abandoned the Lord and served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; now therefore, rescue us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve You.'
verses.12:11: And the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and rescued you from the hand of your enemies all around, and you lived securely.
verses.12:12: But seeing that Nahash, king of the sons of Ammon, had come against you, you said to me, 'By no means; rather, a king will rule over us,' when the Lord your God was reigning over you.
verses.12:13: Now therefore, here stands your king, whom you have chosen and asked for; look, the Lord has given you a king.
verses.12:14: If you fear the Lord, and serve Him, and listen to His voice, and do not provoke the mouth of the Lord, both you and the king who rules over you will be following the Lord your God.
verses.12:15: However, if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord, but provoke His words, the hand of the Lord will be upon you and upon your fathers.
verses.12:16: Now also, stand and see this great thing that the Lord is about to do in your sight.
verses.12:17: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call upon the Lord, and He will give thunder and rain; and you will know and see that you have done a great evil to yourselves in the sight of the Lord by asking for a king over you."
verses.12:18: And Samuel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord gave thunder and rain on that day.
verses.12:19: And all the people feared the Lord and Samuel greatly, and the entire people said to Samuel, "Pray for your servants to the Lord your God, so that we may not die; for we have added an evil to all our sins by asking for a king for ourselves."
verses.12:20: Then Samuel said to the people, "Do not be afraid. You yourselves have done all this evil; nevertheless, do not turn away from behind the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart.
verses.12:21: And do not turn aside after empty things, which will not benefit you nor rescue you, because they are empty.
verses.12:22: And the Lord will not abandon His people for the sake of His great name, because the Lord has sworn to make you a people for Himself.
verses.12:23: Moreover, far be this sin against the Lord from me, that I should cease praying for you; and I will teach you the good and right way.
verses.12:24: Therefore fear the Lord, and serve Him in truth and with your whole heart; for you have seen the magnificent things that He has done among you.
verses.12:25: But if you persist in wickedness, both you and your king will perish together."
verses.13:2: And Saul chose for himself three thousand from Israel; and two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the mountain of Bethel, while one thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin; and as for the rest of the people, he sent them away, each one to his tents.
verses.13:3: And Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Gibeah. And when the Philistines heard of this, Saul sounded the trumpet throughout all the land, saying, "Let the Hebrews hear."
verses.13:4: And all Israel heard a report of this kind: "Saul has struck the garrison of the Philistines, and Israel has risen up against the Philistines." Therefore the people cried out after Saul in Gilgal.
verses.13:5: And the Philistines assembled to do battle against Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and the rest of the multitude as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore. And going up, they encamped in Michmash to the east of Beth-aven.
verses.13:6: When the men of Israel saw that they were placed in tight straits (for the people were distressed), they hid themselves in caves, and in hidden places, in rocks as well, and in caverns, and in cisterns.
verses.13:7: Now the Hebrews crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. And while Saul was still in Gilgal, all the people who were following him were terrified.
verses.13:8: And he waited seven days according to the appointed time of Samuel, yet Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people slipped away from him.
verses.13:9: Therefore Saul said, "Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings." And he offered the burnt offering.
verses.13:10: And when he had finished offering the burnt offering, look, Samuel was coming; and Saul went out to meet him in order to greet him.
verses.13:11: And Samuel spoke to him, "What have you done?" Saul answered, "Because I saw that the people were slipping away from me, and you had not come according to the appointed days, and moreover the Philistines had assembled in Michmash,
verses.13:12: I said, 'Now the Philistines will come down to me in Gilgal, and I have not appeased the face of the Lord.' Compelled by necessity, I offered the burnt offering."
verses.13:13: And Samuel said to Saul, "You have acted foolishly, and you have not kept the commands of the Lord your God that He commanded you. If you had not done this, even now the Lord would have established your kingdom over Israel forever;
verses.13:14: but your kingdom will by no means rise any further. The Lord has sought out for Himself a man according to His own heart, and the Lord has commanded him to be leader over His people, because you have not observed what the Lord commanded."
verses.13:15: Then Samuel rose up and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And the rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the people who were attacking them, coming from Gilgal to Gibeah, on the hill of Benjamin. And Saul counted the people who had been found with him, about six hundred men.
verses.13:16: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people who had been found with them, were in Gibeah of Benjamin, while the Philistines had taken up position in Michmash.
verses.13:17: And three companies went out from the camp of the Philistines to plunder. One company proceeded toward the road to Ophrah, to the land of Shual.
verses.13:18: Moreover, another went along the road to Beth-horon, while the third had turned toward the path of the border overlooking the valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
verses.13:19: Now no blacksmith was found in all the land of Israel, for the Philistines had taken precautions so that the Hebrews would not make a sword or a spear.
verses.13:20: Therefore all Israel used to go down to the Philistines, so that each one might sharpen his plowshare, and his mattock, and his axe, and his hoe.
verses.13:21: And so the edges of the plowshares, and of the mattocks, and of the three-pronged forks, and of the axes were blunted, even to the straightening of a goad.
verses.13:22: And when the day of battle came, neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of all the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, except for Saul and Jonathan his son.
verses.13:23: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to cross over into Michmash.
verses.14:1: And it happened on a certain day that Jonathan the son of Saul said to the young man, his armor-bearer, "Come, and let us cross over to the outpost of the Philistines, which is on the other side of that place." But he did not tell his father this.
verses.14:2: Now Saul was staying in the outermost part of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that was in Migron, and the people with him were about six hundred men.
verses.14:3: And Ahijah the son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, the son of Phinehas, who was descended from Eli, the priest of the Lord in Shiloh, was carrying an ephod. Moreover, the people did not know where Jonathan had gone.
verses.14:4: Now between the ascents by which Jonathan was striving to cross over to the outpost of the Philistines, there were jutting rocks on both sides, and sheer crags, as it were in the shape of teeth, on this side and on that; the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other was Seneh:
verses.14:5: one crag projecting toward the north opposite Michmash, and the other toward the south facing Gibeah.
verses.14:6: Then Jonathan said to the young man, his armor-bearer, "Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men; perhaps the Lord will act for us, for it is not difficult for the Lord to save, whether by many or by few."
verses.14:7: And his armor-bearer said to him, "Do all that pleases your heart; go on where you desire, and I will be with you wherever you wish."
verses.14:8: And Jonathan said, "Look, we are crossing over to those men. And when we appear to them,
verses.14:9: if they speak to us in this way, 'Stay until we come to you,' then let us stand in our place and not go up to them.
verses.14:10: But if they say, 'Come up to us,' let us go up, for the Lord has handed them over into our hands; this will be a sign for us."
verses.14:11: Therefore both of them appeared to the outpost of the Philistines, and the Philistines said, "Look, the Hebrews are coming out of the caves in which they had been hidden."
verses.14:12: And the men from the outpost spoke to Jonathan and to his armor-bearer, and said, "Come up to us, and we will show you something." And Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, "Let us go up; follow me, for the Lord has handed them over into the hands of Israel."
verses.14:13: Then Jonathan climbed up, crawling on hands and feet, and his armor-bearer after him. And so some fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer killed others as he followed him.
verses.14:14: And the first slaughter, with which Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck, was of about twenty men, within half an acre that a pair of oxen is accustomed to plow in a day.
verses.14:15: And a miracle occurred in the camp throughout the fields; moreover, all the people of the outpost of those who had gone to plunder were astounded, and the earth was thrown into turmoil, and it happened like a miracle from God.
verses.14:16: And the watchmen of Saul who were in Gibeah of Benjamin looked out, and look, the multitude was laid low and fleeing this way and that.
verses.14:17: And Saul said to the people who were with him, "Inquire and see who has gone away from us." And when they had inquired, it was found that Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not present.
verses.14:18: And Saul said to Ahijah, "Bring near the ark of God." (For the ark of God was there on that day with the sons of Israel.)
verses.14:19: And while Saul was speaking to the priest, a great uproar arose in the camp of the Philistines, and it was growing little by little and resounding more loudly. And Saul said to the priest, "Withdraw your hand."
verses.14:20: Therefore Saul and all the people who were with him shouted together, and they came all the way to the place of combat; and look, each man's sword had been turned against his neighbor, and there was exceedingly great carnage.
verses.14:21: Moreover, the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines yesterday and the day before, and had gone up with them into the camp, turned back to be with Israel, who were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.14:22: All the Israelites also who had hidden themselves in Mount Ephraim, hearing that the Philistines had fled, joined themselves with their own men in the battle. And there were with Saul about ten thousand men.
verses.14:23: And the Lord saved Israel on that day, and the fight reached as far as Beth-aven.
verses.14:24: And the men of Israel were joined together on that day; and Saul placed the people under an oath, saying, "Cursed is the man who eats bread until evening, until I take vengeance on my enemies." And the entire people ate no bread,
verses.14:25: and all the populace of the land came into a forest, in which there was honey on the surface of the field.
verses.14:26: Therefore the people entered the forest, and flowing honey appeared, and no one brought his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
verses.14:27: Now Jonathan had not heard when his father placed the people under the oath; and he stretched out the tip of the rod that he had in his hand, and dipped it into a honeycomb, and brought his hand back to his mouth, and his eyes were brightened.
verses.14:28: And one of the people answered and said, "Your father bound the people with an oath, saying, 'Cursed is the man who eats bread today.'" (Now the people had grown faint.)
verses.14:29: And Jonathan said, "My father has troubled the land; you yourselves have seen that my eyes were brightened because I tasted a little of this honey;
verses.14:30: how much more if the people had eaten from the plunder of their enemies that they found? Would not a greater slaughter have taken place among the Philistines?"
verses.14:31: Therefore on that day they struck the Philistines from Michmash as far as Aijalon. But the people were exceedingly exhausted;
verses.14:32: and turning to the plunder, they took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate with the blood.
verses.14:33: Then they reported to Saul, saying that the people had sinned against the Lord, eating with the blood. And he said, "You have transgressed; roll a large stone to me right now."
verses.14:34: And Saul said, "Scatter among the populace and tell them that each man bring to me his ox and ram, and kill them on this, and eat, and you will not sin against the Lord by eating with the blood." Therefore all the people brought, each man an ox in his hand, until night, and they killed them there.
verses.14:35: And Saul built an altar to the Lord, and then for the first time he began to build an altar to the Lord.
verses.14:36: And Saul said, "Let us rush upon the Philistines by night, and ravage them until morning dawns, and let us not leave a man of them." And the people said, "Do everything that seems good in your eyes." And the priest said, "Let us draw near here to God."
verses.14:37: And Saul consulted the Lord: "Shall I pursue the Philistines? Will You hand them over into the hands of Israel?" And He did not answer him on that day.
verses.14:38: And Saul said, "Bring here all the corners of the people, and know and see through whom this sin has happened today.
verses.14:39: As the Lord, the Savior of Israel, lives, even if it has been done through Jonathan my son, he will die without retraction." To this no one of all the people contradicted him.
verses.14:40: And he said to all Israel, "Separate yourselves to one side, and I with Jonathan my son will be on the other side." And the people answered Saul, "Do what seems good in your eyes."
verses.14:41: And Saul said to the Lord God of Israel, "Lord God of Israel, give an indication: why is it that You have not answered Your servant today? If this iniquity is in me or in Jonathan my son, give a manifestation; or if this iniquity is in Your people, give holiness." And Jonathan and Saul were caught, but the people went out.
verses.14:42: And Saul said, "Cast the lot between me and Jonathan my son." And Jonathan was taken.
verses.14:43: Then Saul said to Jonathan, "Tell me what you have done." And Jonathan told him and said, "I indeed tasted a little honey on the tip of the rod that was in my hand, and look, I die."
verses.14:44: And Saul said, "May God do these things to me and add these things as well, for you will surely die, Jonathan."
verses.14:45: And the people said to Saul, "Will Jonathan then die, who has accomplished this great salvation in Israel? This is an outrage! As the Lord lives, not a hair from his head will fall to the ground, for he has worked with God today." Therefore the people rescued Jonathan, so that he did not die.
verses.14:46: And Saul withdrew and did not pursue the Philistines; and the Philistines went away to their own places.
verses.14:47: And Saul, when the kingdom over Israel was established, fought all around against all his enemies, against Moab, and the sons of Ammon, and Edom, and the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he prevailed.
verses.14:48: And having gathered an army, he struck Amalek and delivered Israel from the hand of its ravagers.
verses.14:49: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishvi, and Malchishua; and the names of his two daughters: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger was Michal.
verses.14:50: And the name of Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz; and the name of the commander of his army was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's cousin.
verses.14:51: Now Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, was the son of Abiel.
verses.14:52: Now there was fierce war against the Philistines all the days of Saul. For whenever Saul saw any man who was strong and fit for battle, he joined him to himself.
verses.15:1: And Samuel said to Saul, "The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over His people Israel; now therefore listen to the voice of the Lord.
verses.15:2: This is what the Lord of hosts says: 'I have reviewed all that Amalek did to Israel, how he opposed him on the way when he was coming up from Egypt.
verses.15:3: Now therefore go and strike Amalek, and utterly destroy everything that is his; do not spare him, and do not covet anything from his possessions, but kill from man to woman, both little child and nursing infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'"
verses.15:4: So Saul commanded the people and counted them like lambs: two hundred thousand foot soldiers, and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.15:5: And when Saul had come as far as the city of Amalek, he set an ambush in the torrent.
verses.15:6: And Saul said to the Kenites, "Go away, depart, and go down from Amalek, so that I might not perhaps entangle you with him; for you showed mercy to all the sons of Israel when they were coming up from Egypt." And the Kenites departed from the midst of Amalek.
verses.15:7: And Saul struck Amalek from Havilah until you come to Shur, which is opposite Egypt.
verses.15:8: And he captured Agag, king of Amalek, alive; but all the common people he killed with the edge of the sword.
verses.15:9: And Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best flocks of sheep and herds, and the garments and the rams, and everything that was beautiful, and they were unwilling to destroy them; but whatever was inferior and rejected, this they utterly destroyed.
verses.15:10: Now the word of the Lord came to Samuel, saying,
verses.15:11: "I regret that I have appointed Saul as king, because he has abandoned Me and has not fulfilled My words in deed." And Samuel was grieved, and he cried out to the Lord all night.
verses.15:12: And when Samuel had risen in the night to go to Saul in the morning, it was reported to Samuel that Saul had come to Carmel and had erected for himself a triumphal arch, and having turned back, had passed on and gone down to Gilgal. Therefore Samuel came to Saul, and Saul was offering a burnt offering to the Lord from the first of the spoils that he had brought from Amalek.
verses.15:13: And when Samuel had come to Saul, Saul said to him, "Blessed are you by the Lord; I have fulfilled the word of the Lord."
verses.15:14: And Samuel said, "And what is this sound of flocks that resounds in my ears, and of herds that I hear?"
verses.15:15: And Saul said, "They brought them from Amalek; for the people spared the better sheep and herds so that they might be sacrificed to the Lord your God, while the rest we put to death."
verses.15:16: Then Samuel said to Saul, "Allow me, and I will tell you what the Lord spoke to me in the night." And he said to him, "Speak."
verses.15:17: And Samuel said, "When you were small in your own eyes, were you not made head among the tribes of Israel? And the Lord anointed you as king over Israel,
verses.15:18: and the Lord sent you on a journey and said, 'Go and kill the sinners of Amalek, and you will fight against them until their extermination.'
verses.15:19: Why then did you not listen to the voice of the Lord, but turned toward the spoil and did evil in the eyes of the Lord?"
verses.15:20: And Saul said to Samuel, "On the contrary, I did listen to the voice of the Lord, and I walked in the way by which the Lord sent me, and I brought Agag, king of Amalek, and I killed Amalek.
verses.15:21: But the people took sheep and oxen from the spoil, the firstfruits of those that were slaughtered, so that they might sacrifice to the Lord their God in Gilgal."
verses.15:22: And Samuel said, "Does the Lord desire burnt offerings and sacrifices, and not rather that the voice of the Lord be obeyed? For obedience is better than sacrifices, and to listen closely more than to offer the fat of rams.
verses.15:23: For to resist is like the sin of divination, and to refuse to yield is like the crime of idolatry. Therefore, because you have rejected the word of the Lord, the Lord has rejected you from being king."
verses.15:24: And Saul said to Samuel, "I have sinned, because I have transgressed the word of the Lord and your words, fearing the people and obeying their voice.
verses.15:25: But now, please bear my sin, and return with me, so that I may worship the Lord."
verses.15:26: And Samuel said to Saul, "I will not return with you, because you have cast aside the word of the Lord, and the Lord has cast you aside from being king over Israel."
verses.15:27: And Samuel turned around to go away, but he seized the edge of his cloak, which also tore.
verses.15:28: And Samuel said to him, "The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today, and has handed it over to your neighbor who is better than you.
verses.15:29: Moreover, the Victor in Israel will not spare, and will not be swayed by regret; for He is not a man that He should repent."
verses.15:30: Then he said, "I have sinned; yet now honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me, so that I may worship the Lord your God."
verses.15:31: So Samuel returned and followed Saul, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
verses.15:32: And Samuel said, "Bring Agag, king of Amalek, to me." And Agag was brought before him, very fat and trembling. And Agag said, "Does bitter death separate like this?"
verses.15:33: And Samuel said, "Just as your sword has made women childless, so among women your mother will be childless." And Samuel cut him into pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.
verses.15:34: Then Samuel went away to Ramah, while Saul went up to his house in Gibeah.
verses.15:35: And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death; nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul, because the Lord regretted that He had appointed him king over Israel.
verses.16:1: And the Lord said to Samuel, "How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have cast him aside from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and come, so that I may send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite; for I have provided a king for Myself among his sons."
verses.16:2: And Samuel said, "How can I go? For Saul will hear, and he will kill me." And the Lord said, "You will take a calf from the herd in your hand, and you will say, 'I have come to sacrifice to the Lord.'
verses.16:3: And you will call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you should do, and you will anoint whomever I point out to you."
verses.16:4: Therefore Samuel did just as the Lord had spoken to him. And he came to Bethlehem, and the elders of the city were astonished as they came to meet him, and they said, "Is your coming peaceful?"
verses.16:5: And he said, "Peaceful; I have come to sacrifice to the Lord. Sanctify yourselves, and come with me so that I may sacrifice." So he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
verses.16:6: And when they had entered, he saw Eliab and said, "Is His anointed before the Lord?"
verses.16:7: And the Lord said to Samuel, "Do not regard his face or the height of his stature, because I have rejected him, nor do I judge according to the sight of man; for man sees the things that appear, but the Lord looks closely at the heart."
verses.16:8: And Jesse called Abinadab and brought him before Samuel. And he said, "Neither has the Lord chosen this one."
verses.16:9: Then Jesse brought Shammah, of whom he said, "The Lord has not chosen this one either."
verses.16:10: So Jesse brought his seven sons before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, "The Lord has not chosen from among these."
verses.16:11: And Samuel said to Jesse, "Are all the sons already here?" And he answered, "The youngest is still left, and he is tending the sheep." And Samuel said to Jesse, "Send and bring him, for we will not recline at table before he comes here."
verses.16:12: So he sent and brought him. Now he was ruddy, handsome in appearance, and attractive of face; and the Lord said, "Arise, anoint him, for he is the one."
verses.16:13: Therefore Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers, and the Spirit of the Lord was directed upon David from that day onward. And Samuel rose and went away to Ramah.
verses.16:14: Now the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and a wicked spirit from the Lord was tormenting him.
verses.16:15: And the servants of Saul said to him, "Look, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.
verses.16:16: Let our lord command, and your servants who are before you will seek a man who knows how to play the lyre, so that when the evil spirit from the Lord seizes you, he may play with his hand, and you may bear it more easily."
verses.16:17: And Saul said to his servants, "Provide for me, then, someone who plays well, and bring him to me."
verses.16:18: And one of the young men answered and said, "Look, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who knows how to play, very strong in might, a warlike man, prudent in words, and a handsome man; and the Lord is with him."
verses.16:19: Therefore Saul sent messengers to Jesse, saying, "Send to me David your son, who is in the pastures."
verses.16:20: So Jesse took a donkey loaded with loaves of bread, and a flask of wine, and one kid from the goats, and sent them to Saul by the hand of David his son.
verses.16:21: And David came to Saul and stood before him; and he loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.
verses.16:22: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, "Let David stand in my presence, for he has found favor in my eyes."
verses.16:23: Therefore whenever the evil spirit from the Lord seized Saul, David took the lyre and struck it with his hand, and Saul was refreshed and felt better, for the evil spirit departed from him.
verses.17:1: Now the Philistines, gathering their forces for battle, came together at Socoh of Judah, and they encamped between Socoh and Azekah in the borders of Dommim.
verses.17:2: Meanwhile, Saul and the sons of Israel, having gathered together, came into the Valley of the Terebinth, and they drew up the battle line to fight against the Philistines.
verses.17:3: And the Philistines were standing on the mountain on this side, and Israel was standing on the mountain on the other side, and a valley was between them.
verses.17:4: And an illegitimate man came out from the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, from Gath, six cubits and a palm in height.
verses.17:5: And a bronze helmet was on his head, and he was clothed in a scaled coat of armor. Moreover, the weight of his coat of armor was five thousand shekels of bronze.
verses.17:6: And he had bronze greaves on his legs, and a bronze shield covered his shoulders.
verses.17:7: Now the shaft of his spear was like a weavers' beam, and the very iron of his spear had six hundred shekels of iron, and his armor-bearer went ahead of him.
verses.17:8: And standing, he shouted against the battle ranks of Israel and said to them, "Why have you come prepared for battle? Am I not a Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man from among yourselves, and let him come down to single combat.
verses.17:9: If he is able to fight with me and strikes me down, we will be servants to you; but if I prevail and strike him down, you will be servants, and you will serve us."
verses.17:10: And the Philistine said, "I have taunted the forces of Israel today; give me a man, and let him enter into single combat with me."
verses.17:11: Now when Saul and all the Israelites heard such words of the Philistine, they were stunned and were exceedingly afraid.
verses.17:32: When he had been brought to him, he spoke to him, "Let no one's heart fail because of him; I, your servant, will go and fight against the Philistine."
verses.17:33: And Saul said to David, "You are not able to withstand this Philistine, nor to fight against him, because you are a boy, whereas this man has been a warrior from his youth."
verses.17:34: And David said to Saul, "Your servant was tending his father's flock, and a lion or a bear would come and carry off a ram from the middle of the flock,
verses.17:35: and I would pursue them and strike them and rescue it from their mouth; and they would rise up against me, and I would seize their chin, and strangle and kill them.
verses.17:36: For I, your servant, have killed both a lion and a bear; therefore this uncircumcised Philistine also will be like one of them. Now I will go and take away the disgrace of the people; for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, who has dared to curse the army of the living God?"
verses.17:37: And David said, "The Lord, who rescued me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, He Himself will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And Saul said to David, "Go, and may the Lord be with you."
verses.17:38: And Saul dressed David in his own garments, and placed a bronze helmet on his head, and clothed him in a coat of armor.
verses.17:39: So David, having strapped on his sword over his garment, began to test whether he could walk while armed, for he was not accustomed to it. And David said to Saul, "I cannot walk like this, because I have no practice." And he took them off,
verses.17:40: and took his staff, which he always had in his hands, and chose for himself five very smooth stones from the brook, and put them into the shepherd's pouch that he had with him, and took a sling in his hand; and he advanced against the Philistine.
verses.17:42: And when the Philistine looked closely and saw David, he despised him. For he was a youth, ruddy, and handsome in appearance.
verses.17:43: And the Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with a staff?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.17:44: And he said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth."
verses.17:45: But David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with a sword, and a spear, and a shield; but I come to you in the name of the Lord of hosts, the God of the forces of Israel, whom you have taunted
verses.17:46: today, and the Lord will give you into my hand, and I will strike you down and remove your head from you; and I will give the corpses of the camp of the Philistines today to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,
verses.17:47: and this entire assembly may know that the Lord does not save with sword or with spear; for the war is His, and He will give you over into our hands."
verses.17:48: Therefore, when the Philistine had risen and was coming and drawing near against David, David hurried and ran to the fight facing the Philistine.
verses.17:49: And he put his hand into the pouch and took one stone, and hurled it with the sling, and swinging around, struck the Philistine on the forehead; and the stone was embedded in his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
verses.17:51: He ran and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath; and he killed him and cut off his head. Now when the Philistines saw that their mightiest one was dead, they fled.
verses.17:52: And rising up, the men of Israel and Judah shouted aloud and pursued the Philistines until they came into the valley and as far as the gates of Ekron; and the wounded of the Philistines fell on the road of Shaaraim, and as far as Gath, and as far as Ekron.
verses.17:53: And the sons of Israel, returning after they had pursued the Philistines, raided their camp.
verses.17:54: Now David, taking the head of the Philistine, brought it to Jerusalem; but he placed his weapons in his own tent.
verses.18:6: Now when David was returning after the Philistine had been struck down, the women came out from all the cities of Israel, singing and leading dances to meet King Saul, with tambourines of joy and with sistrums.
verses.18:7: And the women led the song, playing and saying, "Saul has struck down a thousand, and David ten thousand."
verses.18:8: Then Saul became exceedingly angry, and this saying was displeasing in his eyes; and he said, "They have given David ten thousand, and to me they have given a thousand; what remains for him, except the kingdom alone?"
verses.18:9: Therefore Saul did not look at David with favorable eyes from that day onward.
verses.18:12: And Saul feared David, because the Lord was with him and had withdrawn from Saul.
verses.18:13: Therefore Saul moved him away from himself and made him a tribune over a thousand men; and he went out and entered in the sight of the people.
verses.18:14: Also in all his ways David acted prudently, and the Lord was with him.
verses.18:15: And so Saul saw that he was exceedingly prudent, and he began to be wary of him.
verses.18:16: But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he himself went in and went out before them.
verses.18:20: Now Michal, the other daughter of Saul, loved David. And it was reported to Saul, and it pleased him.
