verses.18:21: And Saul said, "I will give her to him, so that she may become a stumbling block to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be upon him." And Saul said to David, "In two things you will be my son-in-law today."
verses.18:22: And Saul commanded his servants, "Speak to David secretly from me, saying, 'Look, you please the king, and all his servants love you; now therefore, be the son-in-law of the king.'"
verses.18:23: And the servants of Saul spoke all these words in the ears of David. And David said, "Does it seem a small thing to you to be the son-in-law of the king? Yet I am a poor and lowly man."
verses.18:24: And the servants of Saul reported back, saying, "David spoke words of this kind."
verses.18:25: Then Saul said, "Speak to David like this: 'The king has no need of betrothal gifts, except only a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, so that vengeance may be taken on the enemies of the king.'" However, Saul was planning to give David over into the hands of the Philistines.
verses.18:26: And when his servants had reported back to David the words that Saul had spoken, the saying was pleasing in the eyes of David, that he should become the son-in-law of the king.
verses.18:27: And after a few days, rising up, David departed with the men who were under him. And he struck down two hundred men from the Philistines, and brought their foreskins and counted them out to the king, so that he might be his son-in-law. And so Saul gave him his daughter Michal as a wife.
verses.18:28: And Saul saw and understood that the Lord was with David. And Michal, the daughter of Saul, loved him.
verses.18:29: And Saul began to fear David even more; and Saul became an enemy of David for all days.
verses.19:1: Now Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan, the son of Saul, loved David greatly.
verses.19:2: And Jonathan told David, saying, "Saul my father is seeking to kill you. Therefore, please be on your guard in the morning, and remain in secret and hide yourself.
verses.19:3: I, however, will go out and stand beside my father in the field, wherever you may be, and I will speak about you to my father, and whatever I see, I will report to you."
verses.19:4: Therefore Jonathan spoke good things about David to Saul his father, and he said to him, "Do not sin, king, against your servant David, because he has not sinned against you, and his deeds are very good for you.
verses.19:5: And he put his life in his hand and struck down the Philistine, and the Lord worked a great deliverance for all Israel. You saw it and rejoiced. Why then are you sinning against innocent blood, putting David to death, who is without fault?"
verses.19:6: When Saul heard this, appeased by the voice of Jonathan, he swore, "As the Lord lives, he will not be killed."
verses.19:7: So Jonathan called David and told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David in to Saul, and he was before him just as he had been yesterday and the day before.
verses.19:8: Now war was stirred up again, and David went out and fought against the Philistines, and he struck them with a great blow, and they fled from his presence.
verses.19:9: And an evil spirit of the Lord came upon Saul. Now he was sitting in his house and holding a spear, while David was playing music with his hand.
verses.19:10: And Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David turned aside from Saul's presence, and the spear, with a fruitless blow, was driven into the wall; and David fled and was saved that night.
verses.19:11: Therefore Saul sent his guards to David's house to watch him, so that he would be put to death in the morning. When his wife Michal reported this to David, saying, "Unless you save yourself tonight, tomorrow you will die,"
verses.19:12: she lowered him through a window. And he went away and fled, and was saved.
verses.19:13: Then Michal took a statue and laid it on the bed, and she placed a hairy goatskin at its head and covered it with garments.
verses.19:14: Now Saul sent attendants to seize David, and the answer was given that he was sick.
verses.19:15: And again Saul sent messengers to see David, saying, "Bring him to me in the bed, so that he may be killed."
verses.19:16: And when the messengers came, an image was found on the bed, and a goatskin at its head.
verses.19:17: And Saul said to Michal, "Why have you deceived me like this and let my enemy go, so that he might flee?" And Michal answered Saul, "Because he himself spoke to me, 'Let me go; otherwise I will kill you.'"
verses.19:18: Now David fled and was saved, and he came to Samuel in Ramah and reported to him everything that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went away and stayed in Naioth.
verses.19:19: And it was reported to Saul by those who said, "Look, David is in Naioth in Ramah."
verses.19:20: Therefore Saul sent officers to seize David. When they saw a company of prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing over them, the Spirit of the Lord also came upon them, and they themselves also began to prophesy.
verses.19:21: When this was reported to Saul, he also sent other messengers, and they also prophesied. And again Saul sent a third group of messengers, and they themselves also prophesied. And Saul, enraged with anger,
verses.19:22: went himself also to Ramah, and came as far as the great cistern that is in Socoh. And he inquired and said, "In what place are Samuel and David?" And it was said to him, "Look, they are in Naioth in Ramah."
verses.19:23: And he went to Naioth in Ramah, and the Spirit of the Lord came upon him as well; and he walked along as he went and prophesied until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
verses.19:24: And he himself also stripped off his garments and prophesied with the rest before Samuel, and he fell down naked all that day and night. From this also the proverb went out, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
verses.20:1: Now David fled from Naioth, which is in Ramah, and came and spoke before Jonathan, "What have I done? What is my iniquity, and what is my sin against your father, that he seeks my life?"
verses.20:2: And he said to him, "Far be it! You will not die. For my father will not do anything great or small unless he first tells me. Has my father therefore hidden only this matter from me? That will by no means happen."
verses.20:3: And he swore again to David. And the other said, "Your father surely knows that I have found favor in your eyes, and he will say, 'Let Jonathan not know this, so that he may not be grieved.' Rather, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I and death are separated by only one step, so to speak."
verses.20:4: And Jonathan said to David, "Whatever your soul says to me, I will do for you."
verses.20:5: Then David said to Jonathan, "Look, tomorrow is the new moon, and by custom I usually sit beside the king to eat. Therefore let me go so that I may hide in the field until the evening of the third day.
verses.20:6: If your father looks about and asks for me, you will answer him, 'David asked me to go quickly to Bethlehem, his city, because there are solemn sacrifices there for all his fellow tribesmen.'
verses.20:7: If he says, 'Good,' there will be peace for your servant. But if he is angry, know that his malice is complete.
verses.20:8: Show mercy, therefore, to your servant, because you have caused me, your servant, to enter into a covenant of the Lord with you. But if there is any iniquity in me, put me to death yourself, and do not bring me in to your father."
verses.20:9: And Jonathan said, "Far be this from you! For it cannot happen that, if I know for certain that my father's malice against you is complete, I would not report it to you."
verses.20:10: And David answered Jonathan, "Who will report back to me if your father happens to answer you anything harshly about me?"
verses.20:11: And Jonathan said to David, "Come, and let us go outside into the field." And when both of them had gone out into the field,
verses.20:12: Jonathan said to David, "Lord God of Israel, if I search out my father's intention tomorrow or the day after tomorrow, and there is something good toward David, and I do not immediately send to you and make it known to you,
verses.20:13: may the Lord do these things to Jonathan, and add these as well. But if my father's malice persists against you, I will uncover your ear and send you away, so that you may go in peace; and may the Lord be with you, just as He was with my father.
verses.20:14: And if I live, you will show me the mercy of the Lord; but if I have died,
verses.20:15: you will not remove your mercy from my house forever, when the Lord uproots the enemies of David, every single one from the earth: may He remove Jonathan from his house, and may the Lord require it from the hand of the enemies of David."
verses.20:16: Therefore Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, and the Lord required it from the hand of the enemies of David.
verses.20:17: And Jonathan again swore solemnly to David, because he loved him; for he loved him just as his own soul.
verses.20:18: And Jonathan said to him, "Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed,
verses.20:19: for your seat will be missed until the day after tomorrow. Therefore you will go down quickly and come to the place where you are to be hidden on the day when it is lawful to work, and you will sit beside the stone whose name is Ezel.
verses.20:20: And I will send three arrows beside it, and shoot as if practicing at a target.
verses.20:21: I will also send a boy, saying to him, 'Go and bring me the arrows.'
verses.20:22: If I say to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are on this side of you; take them,' then you come to me, because there is peace for you and there is no harm, as the Lord lives. But if I speak like this to the boy, 'Look, the arrows are beyond you,' go in peace, because the Lord has sent you away.
verses.20:23: Now concerning the word that you and I have spoken, may the Lord be between me and you forever."
verses.20:24: Therefore David hid himself in the field, and the new moon came, and the king sat down to eat bread.
verses.20:25: And when the king had sat down on his seat, according to custom, which was beside the wall, Jonathan stood up, and Abner sat at Saul's side; and David's place appeared empty.
verses.20:26: And Saul did not speak anything on that day, for he thought that perhaps something had happened to him, so that he was not clean nor purified.
verses.20:27: And when the second day after the new moon had dawned, David's place again appeared empty. And Saul said to Jonathan his son, "Why did the son of Jesse come neither yesterday nor today to eat?"
verses.20:28: And Jonathan answered Saul, "He earnestly asked me to go to Bethlehem,
verses.20:29: and he said, 'Let me go, since there is a solemn sacrifice in the city, and one of my brothers has summoned me. Now therefore, if I have found favor in your eyes, I will go quickly and see my brothers.' For this reason he has not come to the king's table."
verses.20:30: Then Saul grew angry against Jonathan and said to him, "Son of a woman who of her own accord seizes a man, am I unaware that you love the son of Jesse to your own shame, and to the shame of your disgraceful mother?
verses.20:31: For all the days that the son of Jesse lives upon the earth, you will not be established, nor will your kingdom. Therefore send right now and bring him to me, because he is a son of death."
verses.20:32: But Jonathan answered Saul his father and said, "Why will he die? What has he done?"
verses.20:33: And Saul seized a spear to strike him. And Jonathan understood that it had been determined by his father to put David to death.
verses.20:34: Therefore Jonathan rose from the table in furious anger, and he did not eat bread on the second day of the new moon. For he was grieved over David, because his father had shamed him.
verses.20:35: And when morning had dawned, Jonathan came into the field according to the appointment with David, and a small boy was with him.
verses.20:36: And he said to his boy, "Go and bring me the arrows that I shoot." And when the boy had run, he shot another arrow past the boy.
verses.20:37: So the boy came to the place of the arrow that Jonathan had shot, and Jonathan called out behind the boy's back and said, "Look, the arrow is there, farther beyond you."
verses.20:38: And Jonathan called out again behind the boy's back, saying, "Hurry quickly; do not stand still!" So Jonathan's boy gathered the arrows and brought them to his master.
verses.20:39: And he was completely unaware of what was being done, for only Jonathan and David knew the matter.
verses.20:40: Therefore Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and said to him, "Go and carry them into the city."
verses.20:41: And when the boy had gone away, David rose from the place that faced toward the south, and falling facedown to the ground, he bowed down three times. And kissing one another, they wept together, but David even more.
verses.20:42: Therefore Jonathan said to David, "Go in peace: whatever we both have sworn in the name of the Lord, saying, 'May the Lord be between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring forever.'"
verses.21:1: And David rose and departed, and Jonathan also entered the city.
verses.21:2: Now David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest, and Ahimelech was astonished because David had come. And he said to him, "Why are you alone, and no one is with you?"
verses.21:3: And David said to Ahimelech the priest, "The king has charged me with a matter and said, 'Let no one know the matter for which you have been sent by me, and what kind of commands I have given you.' For I have also appointed the young men to meet at such and such a place.
verses.21:4: Now therefore, if you have anything at hand, at least five loaves of bread, give them to me, or whatever you find."
verses.21:5: And the priest answered David and said to him, "I do not have common loaves at hand, but only holy bread—if the young men are clean, especially from women?"
verses.21:6: And David answered the priest and said to him, "Indeed, if it is a question of women, we have abstained since yesterday and the day before yesterday when we set out, and the vessels of the young men were holy. Moreover, this journey is defiled, yet even it will be sanctified today in the vessels."
verses.21:7: The priest therefore gave him sanctified bread; for there was no bread there except the loaves of presentation alone, which had been removed from the presence of the Lord so that warm loaves might be set out.
verses.21:8: Now a certain man from among the servants of Saul was there on that day, inside the tabernacle of the Lord; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the mightiest of the shepherds of Saul.
verses.21:9: And David said to Ahimelech, "Do you have a spear or a sword here at hand? For I did not bring my sword and my weapons with me, since the king's matter was urgent."
verses.21:10: And the priest said, "Here is the sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you struck down in the Valley of the Terebinth; it is wrapped in a cloak behind the ephod. If you wish to take that one, take it, for there is no other here besides it." And David said, "There is no other like this one; give it to me."
verses.21:11: David therefore rose and fled on that day from the presence of Saul, and came to Achish, king of Gath.
verses.21:12: And the servants of Achish said to him when they had seen David, "Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing of him in dances, saying, 'Saul struck down a thousand, and David ten thousand'?"
verses.21:13: Now David placed these words in his heart, and he was greatly afraid in the presence of Achish, king of Gath.
verses.21:14: And he changed his face before them and kept collapsing between their hands, and he kept striking against the doors of the gate, and his saliva flowed down onto his beard.
verses.21:15: And Achish said to his servants, "You have seen an insane man; why have you brought him to me?
verses.21:16: Do we lack raving madmen, that you have brought this one in to rave in my presence? Will this man enter my house?"
verses.22:1: David therefore departed from there and fled into the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and all his father's house heard of this, they went down to him there.
verses.22:2: And all who were caught in distress, and oppressed by debt, and bitter in spirit gathered to him; and he became their leader, and about four hundred men were with him.
verses.22:3: And David set out from there to Mizpah, which belongs to Moab, and said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother stay with you, until I know what God will do for me."
verses.22:4: And he left them in the presence of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him all the days that David was in the stronghold.
verses.22:5: And Gad the prophet said to David, "Do not stay in the stronghold; set out and go into the land of Judah." And David set out and came into the forest of Hereth.
verses.22:6: And Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had appeared. Now while Saul was staying in Gibeah and was in the grove that is in Ramah, holding a spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him,
verses.22:7: he said to his servants who were standing by him, "Listen now, sons of Jemini: will the son of Jesse give fields and vineyards to all of you, and make all of you tribunes and centurions?
verses.22:8: For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who reports to me, especially since my son also has entered into a covenant with the son of Jesse. There is no one among you who grieves over my plight, nor anyone who informs me, because my son has stirred up my servant against me, lying in wait for me to this day."
verses.22:9: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing by and was foremost among the servants of Saul, answered and said, "I saw the son of Jesse in Nob, with Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, the priest.
verses.22:10: He consulted the Lord for him and gave him provisions, and he also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine."
verses.22:11: The king therefore sent to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father's house, the priests who were in Nob; and they all came to the king.
verses.22:12: And Saul said to Ahimelech, "Listen, son of Ahitub." And he answered, "I am ready, my lord."
verses.22:13: And Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, and given him loaves of bread and a sword, and consulted God for him, so that he might rise up against me, remaining one who lies in wait to this day?"
verses.22:14: And Ahimelech answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants is like David—faithful, and the king's son-in-law, and going at your command, and honored in your house?
verses.22:15: Did I begin today to consult God for him? Far be this from me! Let the king not suspect a thing of this kind against his servant, in all my father's house; for your servant knew nothing about this affair, either small or great."
verses.22:16: And the king said, "You will certainly die, Ahimelech, you and all your father's house."
verses.22:17: And the king said to the emissaries who stood around him, "Turn and kill the priests of the Lord, for their hand is with David; knowing that he had fled, yet they did not inform me." But the servants of the king were unwilling to stretch out their hands against the priests of the Lord.
verses.22:18: And the king said to Doeg, "You turn and rush upon the priests." And Doeg the Edomite turned and rushed upon the priests, and slaughtered on that day eighty-five men clothed in a linen ephod.
verses.22:19: And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword: men and women, and little children and nursing infants, and ox, donkey, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
verses.22:20: Now one son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled to David,
verses.22:21: and reported to him that Saul had killed the priests of the Lord.
verses.22:22: And David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day, since Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would without doubt report it to Saul; I am guilty of all the souls of your father.
verses.22:23: Stay with me; do not be afraid: if anyone seeks my life, he will seek your life also, and with me you will be kept safe."
verses.23:1: And they told David, saying, "Look, the Philistines are attacking Keilah and plundering the threshing floors."
verses.23:2: David therefore consulted the Lord, saying, "Should I go and strike these Philistines?" And the Lord said to David, "Go, and you will strike the Philistines and save Keilah."
verses.23:3: And the men who were with David said to him, "Look, we are afraid while staying here in Judea; how much more if we go to Keilah against the ranks of the Philistines?"
verses.23:4: David therefore consulted the Lord again. And answering, He said to him, "Rise and go to Keilah, for I will deliver the Philistines into your hand."
verses.23:5: David and his men therefore went to Keilah, and he fought against the Philistines, and drove off their livestock, and struck them with a great blow; and David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
verses.23:6: Now at the time when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech was fleeing to David in Keilah, he had come down having an ephod with him.
verses.23:7: Now it was reported to Saul that David had come to Keilah, and Saul said, "God has delivered him into my hands, and he is shut in, having entered a city in which there are gates and bars."
verses.23:8: And Saul commanded all the people to go down to Keilah for battle and to besiege David and his men.
verses.23:9: When David learned that Saul was secretly preparing evil against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod near."
verses.23:10: And David said, "Lord God of Israel, Your servant has heard a report that Saul intends to come to Keilah to destroy the city on account of me:
verses.23:11: will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hands? And will Saul come down, just as Your servant has heard? Lord God of Israel, tell Your servant." And the Lord said, "He will come down."
verses.23:13: David and his men, about six hundred, therefore rose, and having gone out from Keilah, they wandered here and there uncertainly; and it was reported to Saul that David had fled from Keilah and had escaped; for this reason he refrained from going out.
verses.23:14: Now David stayed in the desert in the strongest places, and remained on the mountain of the wilderness of Ziph, on a shaded mountain; yet Saul sought him every day, and God did not deliver him into his hands.
verses.23:15: And David saw that Saul had gone out to seek his life. Now David was in the desert of Ziph, in a forest.
verses.23:16: And Jonathan the son of Saul rose and went to David into the forest, and strengthened his hands in God, and said to him,
verses.23:17: "Do not be afraid, for the hand of my father Saul will not find you; and you will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you; and my father Saul also knows this."
verses.23:18: Both of them therefore made a covenant before the Lord; and David remained in the forest, while Jonathan returned to his house.
verses.23:19: Now the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Look, is David not hiding among us in the safest places of the forest, on the hill of Hachilah, which is to the right of the desert?
verses.23:20: Now therefore, just as your soul has desired to come down, come down; and it will be our part to deliver him into the hands of the king."
verses.23:21: And Saul said, "May you be blessed by the Lord, because you have grieved over my plight.
verses.23:22: Go therefore, please, and prepare more diligently, and inquire more closely, and observe the place where his foot is, or who has seen him there; for he thinks about me that I craftily lie in wait for him.
verses.23:23: Observe and see all his hiding places in which he hides himself, and return to me with certainty, so that I may go with you. And if he even hides himself in the earth, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah."
verses.23:24: So rising, they went to Ziph ahead of Saul; now David and his men were in the desert of Maon, in the plains to the right of Jeshimon.
verses.23:25: Saul and his companions therefore went to seek him. And it was reported to David, and immediately he went down to the rock and stayed in the desert of Maon; and when Saul heard of this, he pursued David in the desert of Maon.
verses.23:26: And Saul was going along the side of the mountain on one side, while David and his men were on the side of the mountain on the other side. Moreover, David was despairing of being able to escape from the presence of Saul; and so Saul and his men were encircling David and his men in the form of a ring, in order to capture them.
verses.23:27: And a messenger came to Saul, saying, "Hurry and come, for the Philistines have poured themselves over the land."
verses.23:28: Saul therefore turned back, ceasing to pursue David, and proceeded to meet the Philistines; on account of this they called that place the Dividing Rock.
verses.24:1: So David went up from there and lived in the most secure places of En-gedi.
verses.24:2: And when Saul had returned after he pursued the Philistines, they reported to him, saying, "Look, David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."
verses.24:3: Therefore, taking three thousand chosen men from all Israel, Saul set out to search for David and his men, even over the steepest crags, which are passable only to wild goats.
verses.24:4: And he came to sheepfolds that presented themselves to a traveler, and there was a cave there, which Saul entered to relieve his bowels. Meanwhile David and his men were hiding in the inner part of the cave.
verses.24:5: And David's servants said to him, "Here is the day of which the Lord spoke to you: 'I will hand your enemy over to you, so that you may do to him as is pleasing in your eyes.'" So David rose up and silently cut off the hem of Saul's cloak.
verses.24:6: After these things, David's heart struck him because he had cut off the hem of Saul's cloak.
verses.24:7: And he said to his men, "May the Lord be merciful to me, that I should not do this thing to my lord, the anointed of the Lord, to lay my hand against him, because he is the anointed of the Lord."
verses.24:8: And David subdued his men with words and did not allow them to rise up against Saul. Meanwhile Saul, rising up from the cave, proceeded on the journey he had begun.
verses.24:9: Then David also rose up after him, and going out of the cave, he called out behind Saul's back, saying, "My lord the king." And Saul looked back behind him, and David, bowing himself face down to the ground, paid homage.
verses.24:10: And he said to Saul, "Why do you listen to the words of men who say, 'David seeks evil against you'?
verses.24:11: Look, today your eyes have seen that the Lord handed you over into my hand in the cave. And I thought to kill you, but my eye spared you; for I said, 'I will not stretch out my hand against my lord, because he is the anointed of the Lord.'
verses.24:12: Moreover, my father, look and recognize the hem of your cloak in my hand; for when I cut off the edge of your cloak, I was unwilling to stretch out my hand against you. Take note and see that there is no evil or iniquity in my hand, nor have I sinned against you; yet you lie in wait for my life to take it away.
verses.24:13: May the Lord judge between me and you, and may the Lord avenge me on you; but let my hand not be against you.
verses.24:14: Just as it is also said in the ancient proverb, 'From the wicked, wickedness will come forth.' Therefore let my hand not be against you.
verses.24:15: Whom are you pursuing, king of Israel? Whom are you pursuing? You are pursuing a dead dog, and a single flea.
verses.24:16: May the Lord be judge, and judge between me and you; and may He see, and judge my cause, and rescue me from your hand."
verses.24:17: Now when David had finished speaking words of this kind to Saul, Saul said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And Saul lifted up his voice and wept.
verses.24:18: And he said to David, "You are more righteous than I; for you have rendered good things to me, whereas I have repaid evil things to you.
verses.24:19: And you have shown today what good things you have done for me: how the Lord handed me over into your hand, and you did not kill me.
verses.24:20: For who, when he finds his enemy, will let him go on a good way? Instead, may the Lord repay you this recompense for what you have done toward me today.
verses.24:21: And now, because I know that you will most certainly reign and will hold the kingdom of Israel in your hand,
verses.24:22: swear to me by the Lord that you will not blot out my offspring after me, nor remove my name from my father's house."
verses.24:23: And David swore to Saul. So Saul departed to his house, and David and his men went up to more secure places.
verses.25:1: Now Samuel died, and all Israel was gathered together, and they mourned for him and buried him in his house in Ramah. And rising up, David went down into the wilderness of Paran.
verses.25:2: Now there was a certain man in the desert of Maon, and his property was in Carmel, and that man was exceedingly great. He had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats; and it happened that his flock was being sheared in Carmel.
verses.25:3: Now the name of that man was Nabal, and the name of his wife was Abigail. That woman was most prudent and beautiful, whereas her husband was harsh, very wicked, and malicious; and he was of the lineage of Caleb.
verses.25:4: Therefore, when David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his flock,
verses.25:5: he sent ten young men and said to them, "Go up to Carmel, and you will come to Nabal and greet him peacefully in my name.
verses.25:6: And you will say, 'May peace be to my brothers and to you, and peace to your house, and may peace be to all things that you have.
verses.25:7: I have heard that your shepherds, who were with us in the wilderness, are shearing. We were never troublesome to them, nor was anything from the flock ever missing for them during all the time that they were with us in Carmel.
verses.25:8: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. Now therefore let your young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a good day. Whatever your hand finds, give to your servants and to your son David.'"
verses.25:9: And when David's young men had come, they spoke all these words to Nabal in David's name, and they fell silent.
verses.25:10: But Nabal, answering David's young men, said, "Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? Today servants who flee from their masters have multiplied.
verses.25:11: Should I therefore take my loaves of bread, and my water, and the meat of the livestock that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to men when I do not know where they are from?"
verses.25:12: Accordingly, David's young men went back along their way, and returning, they came and reported to him all the words that he had spoken.
verses.25:13: Then David said to his young men, "Let each man strap on his sword." And each of them strapped on his sword, and David also strapped on his sword. And about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred remained with the baggage.
verses.25:14: Now one of her young men reported to Abigail, Nabal's wife, saying, "Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to bless our master, and he spurned them.
verses.25:15: Those men had been very good to us and not troublesome, nor was anything ever lost during all the time that we associated with them in the wilderness.
verses.25:16: They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the days that we pastured the flocks near them.
verses.25:17: For this reason, consider and think over what you should do, because evil is complete against your husband and against your house, and he himself is a son of Belial, so that no one can speak to him."
verses.25:18: Therefore Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, and two skins of wine, and five cooked rams, and five measures of parched grain, and one hundred bundles of raisins, and two hundred cakes of dried figs, and placed them on donkeys.
verses.25:19: And she said to her young men, "Go ahead of me; look, I will follow behind you." However, she did not tell her husband Nabal.
verses.25:20: So when she had mounted a donkey and was going down to the foot of the mountain, David and his men were coming down to meet her, and she also met them.
verses.25:21: And David said, "Truly in vain I guarded everything that belonged to this man in the wilderness, and nothing was lost from all that pertained to him; and he has repaid me evil for good.
verses.25:22: May God do these things to the enemies of David, and add these things as well, if I leave until morning, out of all that belongs to him, one who urinates against a wall."
verses.25:23: Now when Abigail saw David, she hurried and got down from the donkey, and fell down before David on her face, and paid homage on the ground.
verses.25:24: And she fell at his feet and said, "On me, my lord, let this iniquity be. Let your maidservant speak, I beg you, in your ears, and listen to the words of your female servant.
verses.25:25: Please, let my lord the king not set his heart upon this wicked man Nabal, because according to his name he is a fool, and folly is with him. But I, your maidservant, did not see your young men, my lord, whom you sent.
verses.25:26: Now therefore, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, He who kept you from coming to bloodshed and saved your hand for you: now let your enemies, and those who seek evil for my lord, become like Nabal.
verses.25:27: Therefore accept this blessing that your maidservant has brought to you, my lord, and give it to the young men who follow you, my lord.
verses.25:28: Take away the iniquity of your female servant; for the Lord will surely make for you, my lord, a faithful house, because you fight the battles of the Lord, my lord. Therefore let evil not be found in you all the days of your life.
verses.25:29: For if at any time a man rises up pursuing you and seeking your life, the life of my lord will be kept safe as in the bundle of the living with the Lord your God; whereas the life of your enemies will be whirled around, as in the force and circle of a sling.
verses.25:30: Therefore, when the Lord has done for you, my lord, all the good things that He has spoken concerning you, and has appointed you leader over Israel,
verses.25:31: this will not be a sobbing and a scruple of heart for you, my lord, that you shed innocent blood or avenged yourself. And when the Lord has done good to my lord, you will remember your maidservant."
verses.25:32: And David said to Abigail, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who sent you today to meet me, and blessed be your speech,
verses.25:33: and blessed be you, who kept me today from going to bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.
verses.25:34: Otherwise, as the Lord God of Israel lives, who kept me from doing evil to you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, there would not have remained to Nabal until the morning light one who urinates against a wall."
verses.25:35: Therefore David received from her hand everything that she had brought him, and said to her, "Go peacefully to your house; look, I have listened to your voice and have honored your face."
verses.25:36: Now Abigail came to Nabal, and look, he had a banquet in his house like the banquet of a king, and Nabal's heart was merry, for he was exceedingly drunk. And she did not tell him a word, small or great, until morning.
verses.25:37: At daybreak, however, when Nabal had digested the wine, his wife told him these words; and his heart died within him, and he became like a stone.
verses.25:38: And when ten days had passed, the Lord struck Nabal, and he died.
verses.25:39: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, "Blessed be the Lord, who has judged the cause of my reproach from the hand of Nabal, and has kept His servant from evil, and the Lord has returned the evil of Nabal upon his head." Therefore David sent and spoke to Abigail, to take her for himself as a wife.
verses.25:40: And David's young men came to Abigail in Carmel and spoke to her, saying, "David has sent us to you, to take you for himself as a wife."
verses.25:41: And rising up, she paid homage face down to the ground and said, "Look, let your female servant be a maidservant, to wash the feet of the servants of my lord."
verses.25:42: And Abigail hurried and rose up, and mounted a donkey, and five young women, her attendants, went with her; and she followed David's messengers, and she became his wife.
verses.25:43: Moreover, David also took Ahinoam from Jezreel, and each of the two was his wife.
verses.25:44: Now Saul gave his daughter Michal, David's wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
verses.26:1: And the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, "Look, David is hidden on the hill of Hachilah, which is opposite the wasteland."
verses.26:2: And Saul rose and went down into the wilderness of Ziph, and with him three thousand men from the chosen of Israel, to search for David in the wilderness of Ziph.
verses.26:3: And Saul encamped at Gibeah of Hachilah, which was opposite the wasteland on the road, while David was dwelling in the wilderness. And seeing that Saul had come after him into the wilderness,
verses.26:4: he sent scouts and learned that he had most certainly come there.
verses.26:5: And David rose secretly and came to the place where Saul was; and when he had seen the place in which Saul was sleeping, and Abner the son of Ner, the commander of his army, and Saul sleeping in the tent, and the rest of the crowd around him,
verses.26:6: David spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, saying, "Who will go down with me to Saul into the camp?" And Abishai said, "I will go down with you."
verses.26:7: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and they found Saul lying and sleeping in the tent, with a spear fixed in the ground at his head, while Abner and the people were sleeping around him.
verses.26:8: And Abishai said to David, "God has shut your enemy into your hands today; now therefore let me pierce him to the ground with the lance once, and there will be no need a second time."
verses.26:9: And David said to Abishai, "Do not kill him, for who will stretch out his hand against the anointed of the Lord and be innocent?"
verses.26:10: And David said, "As the Lord lives, unless the Lord strikes him, or his day comes to die, or going down into battle he perishes,
verses.26:11: may the Lord be merciful to me so that I do not stretch out my hand against the anointed of the Lord. Now therefore take the spear that is at his head and the cup of water, and let us go."
verses.26:12: So David took the spear and the cup of water that was at Saul's head, and they went away; and there was no one who saw, or perceived, or woke up, but all of them were sleeping, because a deep sleep from the Lord had fallen upon them.
verses.26:13: And when David had crossed over to the opposite side, and stood on the top of the mountain from afar, and there was a great space between them,
verses.26:14: David called out to the people and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, "Will you not answer, Abner?" And Abner answered and said, "Who are you, who call out and disturb the king?"
verses.26:15: And David said to Abner, "Are you not a man? And who else is like you in Israel? Why then have you not guarded your lord the king? For one of the crowd came in to kill the king your lord.
verses.26:16: This is not good, what you have done. As the Lord lives, you are sons of death, you who have not guarded your lord, the anointed of the Lord. Now therefore see where the king's spear is, and where the cup of water is that was at his head."
verses.26:17: And Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is this your voice, my son David?" And David said, "It is my voice, my lord the king."
verses.26:18: And he said, "For what reason does my lord pursue his servant? What have I done? Or what evil is in my hand?
verses.26:19: Now therefore hear, I ask you, my lord the king, the words of your servant: if the Lord incites you against me, let Him smell a sacrifice; but if the sons of men, cursed are they in the sight of the Lord, who have driven me out today so that I should not dwell in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, 'Go, serve foreign gods.'
verses.26:20: And now let not my blood be poured out on the ground before the Lord, for the king of Israel has come out to search for a single flea, just as a partridge is pursued in the mountains."
verses.26:21: And Saul said, "I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will never again do you harm, because my life has been precious in your eyes today; for it is clear that I have acted foolishly and have been ignorant of very many things."
verses.26:22: And David answered and said, "Here is the king's spear; let one of the king's young men cross over and take it.
verses.26:23: And the Lord will repay each one according to his righteousness and faithfulness, for the Lord delivered you today into my hand, and I was unwilling to stretch out my hand against the anointed of the Lord.
verses.26:24: And just as your life has been magnified today in my eyes, so may my life be magnified in the eyes of the Lord, and may He deliver me from all distress."
verses.26:25: Therefore Saul said to David, "Blessed are you, my son David; and indeed you will surely act, and you will surely prevail." And David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.
verses.27:1: And David said in his heart, "Sometime, one day, I will fall into the hands of Saul. Is it not better that I flee and be saved in the land of the Philistines, so that Saul will despair and stop searching for me within all the borders of Israel? Therefore I will escape his hands."
verses.27:2: And David rose and went, he and six hundred men with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.
verses.27:3: And David dwelt with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each man and his household, and David and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
verses.27:4: And it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath, and he did not continue searching for him any longer.
verses.27:5: And David said to Achish, "If I have found favor in your eyes, let a place be given to me in one of the towns of this region, so that I may dwell there; for why does your servant remain in the city of the king with you?"
verses.27:6: Therefore Achish gave him Ziklag on that day; for this reason Ziklag came to belong to the kings of Judah until this day.
verses.27:7: And the number of the days during which David dwelt in the region of the Philistines was four months.
verses.27:8: And David and his men went up and carried off plunder from the Geshurites, and from the Girzites, and from the Amalekites; for these districts were inhabited in the land from ancient times, as one goes to Shur, as far as the land of Egypt.
verses.27:9: And David would strike the whole land, and would not leave man or woman alive; and taking sheep, and oxen, and donkeys, and camels, and garments, he would return and come to Achish.
verses.27:10: And Achish would say to him, "Against whom have you raided today?" David would answer, "Against the south of Judah, and against the south of Jerahmeel, and against the south of the Kenites."
verses.27:11: Neither man nor woman would David keep alive, nor bring to Gath, saying, "Otherwise they might speak against us, 'David has done these things.'" And this was his decree all the days during which he dwelt in the region of the Philistines.
verses.27:12: Therefore Achish believed David, saying, "He has worked many evils against his people Israel; therefore he will be my perpetual servant."
verses.28:1: And it happened in those days that the Philistines gathered their armies to prepare for war against Israel; and Achish said to David, "Now know for certain that you will go out with me in the camp, you and your men."
verses.28:2: And David said to Achish, "Now you will know what your servant is about to do." And Achish said to David, "And I will appoint you guardian of my head for all days."
verses.28:3: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him in Ramah, his city. And Saul had removed the magicians and soothsayers from the land.
verses.28:4: And the Philistines assembled, and came, and encamped at Shunem; and Saul also gathered all Israel, and came to Gilboa.
verses.28:5: And Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, and he was afraid, and his heart was exceedingly terrified.
verses.28:6: And he consulted the Lord, and He did not answer him, neither through dreams, nor through priests, nor through prophets.
verses.28:7: And Saul said to his servants, "Search for a woman for me who has a divining spirit, and I will go to her and inquire through her." And his servants said to him, "There is a woman who has a divining spirit at Endor."
verses.28:8: So he changed his appearance and put on other garments, and he went, he and two men with him; and they came to the woman by night, and he said to her, "Divine for me by the divining spirit, and raise up for me the one whom I tell you."
verses.28:9: And the woman said to him, "Look, you know how much Saul has done, and how he has wiped out the magicians and soothsayers from the land; why then do you lay a snare for my life, so that I may be killed?"
verses.28:10: And Saul swore to her by the Lord, saying, "As the Lord lives, no evil at all will happen to you because of this matter."
verses.28:11: And the woman said to him, "Whom shall I raise up for you?" And he said, "Raise up Samuel for me."
verses.28:12: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice and said to Saul, "Why have you deceived me? For you are Saul."
verses.28:13: And the king said to her, "Do not be afraid. What did you see?" And the woman said to Saul, "I saw gods ascending out of the earth."
verses.28:14: And he said to her, "What is his appearance?" And she said, "An old man is ascending, and he is wrapped in a cloak." And Saul understood that it was Samuel, and he bowed himself upon his face to the ground and paid homage.
verses.28:15: And Samuel said to Saul, "Why have you disturbed me, so that I should be raised up?" And Saul said, "I am exceedingly distressed, for the Philistines are fighting against me, and God has departed from me and has been unwilling to answer me, neither by the hand of prophets nor through dreams; therefore I have called you, so that you may show me what I should do."
verses.28:16: And Samuel said, "Why do you question me, since the Lord has departed from you and has passed over to your rival?
verses.28:17: For the Lord will do to you just as He spoke by my hand, and He will tear your kingdom from your hand and will give it to your neighbor David,
verses.28:18: because you did not obey the voice of the Lord, nor did you carry out the wrath of His fury against Amalek; therefore what you are suffering, the Lord has done to you today.
verses.28:19: And the Lord will also give Israel with you into the hands of the Philistines, and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me; and moreover the Lord will deliver the camp of Israel into the hands of the Philistines."
verses.28:20: And immediately Saul fell stretched out upon the ground, for he was terrified by the words of Samuel, and there was no strength in him, because he had not eaten bread all that day.
verses.28:21: Then that woman came in to Saul (for he was greatly troubled) and said to him, "Look, your maidservant has obeyed your voice, and I have placed my life in my hand, and I have listened to your words that you spoke to me.
verses.28:22: Now therefore, you also listen to the voice of your maidservant, and I will set before you a morsel of bread, so that by eating you may regain strength and be able to travel."
verses.28:23: But he refused and said, "I will not eat." However, his servants and the woman pressed him, and at last, having listened to their voice, he rose from the ground and sat on the bed.
verses.28:24: Now that woman had a pasture-fed calf in the house, and she hurried and killed it; and taking flour, she mixed it and baked unleavened bread,
verses.28:25: and set it before Saul and before his servants. And when they had eaten, they rose and walked throughout that whole night.
verses.29:1: So all the divisions of the Philistines were gathered together in Aphek, and Israel also encamped by the spring that was in Jezreel.
verses.29:2: And the satraps of the Philistines were marching in hundreds and in thousands, while David and his men were in the rear division with Achish.
verses.29:3: And the leaders of the Philistines said to Achish, "What do these Hebrews want?" And Achish said to the leaders of the Philistines, "Are you unaware of David, who was the servant of Saul, king of Israel, and has been with me for many days, or years, and I have not found anything in him from the day on which he defected to me until this day?"
verses.29:4: But the leaders of the Philistines became angry with him and said to him, "Let this man return and stay in his place where you appointed him, and let him not go down with us into battle, so that he does not become an adversary to us when we begin to fight; for how else will he be able to appease his master, except with our heads?
verses.29:5: Is this not David, for whom they sang in dances, saying, 'Saul has struck in his thousands, and David in his ten thousands'?"
verses.29:6: So Achish called David and said to him, "As the Lord lives, you are upright and good in my sight, and your going out and your coming in are with me in the camp; and I have not found anything evil in you from the day on which you came to me until this day; but you do not please the satraps.
verses.29:7: Therefore return, and go in peace, and do not offend the eyes of the satraps of the Philistines."
verses.29:8: And David said to Achish, "For what have I done, and what have you found in me, your servant, from the day on which I have been in your sight until this day, that I should not come and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?"
verses.29:9: Then Achish answered and spoke to David, "I know that you are good in my eyes, like an angel of God; but the leaders of the Philistines have said, 'He will not go up with us into battle.'
verses.29:10: Therefore rise up in the morning, you and the servants of your master who came with you; and when you have risen while it is still night and it begins to grow light, depart."
verses.29:11: So David rose while it was still night, he and his men, to set out in the morning and return to the land of the Philistines; but the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.30:1: Now when David and his men had come to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made an attack from the southern side against Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag and burned it with fire.
verses.30:2: And they had led the women away captive from it, from the least to the great; and they had not killed anyone, but had led them along with them and were going on their way.
verses.30:3: So when David and his men came to the city and found it burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and daughters led away captive,
verses.30:4: David and the people who were with him lifted up their voices and wept until tears failed in them.
verses.30:5: Indeed, the two wives of David had also been led away captive: Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail, the wife of Nabal of Carmel.
verses.30:6: And David was deeply grieved, for the people wanted to stone him, because the soul of every man was bitter over his sons and daughters; but David was strengthened in the Lord his God.
verses.30:7: And he said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, "Bring the ephod to me." And Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
verses.30:8: And David consulted the Lord, saying, "Should I pursue these raiders, and will I overtake them, or not?" And the Lord said to him, "Pursue, for without a doubt you will overtake them and recover the plunder."
verses.30:9: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came as far as the Besor stream; and some who were exhausted stayed behind.
verses.30:10: But David himself and four hundred men pursued, for two hundred had stayed behind who, being exhausted, could not cross the Besor stream.
verses.30:11: And they found an Egyptian man in the field and brought him to David; and they gave him bread to eat and water to drink,
verses.30:12: and also a piece of a cake of dried figs and two bunches of raisins. When he had eaten these, his spirit returned and he was revived, for he had not eaten bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights.
verses.30:13: Then David said to him, "To whom do you belong? Or where are you from? And where are you going?" And he said, "I am an Egyptian youth, the servant of an Amalekite man; and my master abandoned me because I began to fall ill the day before yesterday.
verses.30:14: Indeed, we made a raid against the southern region of the Cherethites, and against Judah, and against the south of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire."
verses.30:15: And David said to him, "Can you lead me to this band?" And he said, "Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and will not hand me over into the hands of my master, and I will lead you to this band." And David swore to him.
verses.30:16: And when he had led him, look, they were reclining over the face of the whole land, eating and drinking, and as though celebrating a festival day, because of all the plunder and spoils that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
verses.30:17: And David struck them down from evening until the evening of the next day, and not one of them escaped, except four hundred young men who had mounted camels and fled.
verses.30:18: So David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and he recovered his two wives.
verses.30:19: Nor was anything missing, from small to great, both of the sons and of the daughters, and of the spoils, and whatever they had seized; David brought back everything.
verses.30:20: And he took all the flocks and herds, and drove them before his face; and they said, "This is David's plunder."
verses.30:21: Then David came to the two hundred men who, being exhausted, had stayed behind and had not been able to follow David, and he had ordered them to remain at the Besor stream; and they went out to meet David and the people who were with him. And David, approaching the people, greeted them peacefully.
verses.30:22: And every vile and unjust man among the men who had gone with David answered and said, "Because they did not come with us, we will not give them anything of the plunder that we recovered; rather, let his wife and children be enough for each one, and when they have taken them, let them depart."
verses.30:23: But David said, "You must not do so, my brothers, concerning the things that the Lord has delivered to us; and He has guarded us and given the raiders who had made a raid against us into our hands;
verses.30:24: nor will anyone listen to you concerning this matter; for the share of the one who goes down to battle and of the one who remains by the baggage will be equal, and they will divide alike."
verses.30:25: And from that day onward this became established and prescribed, and like a law in Israel until this day.
verses.30:26: So David came to Ziklag and sent gifts from the plunder to the elders of Judah, his neighbors, saying, "Receive a blessing from the plunder of the enemies of the Lord,"
verses.30:27: to those who were in Bethel, and those in Ramoth toward the south, and those in Jether,
verses.30:28: and those in Aroer, and those in Siphmoth, and those in Eshtemoa,
verses.30:29: and those in Racal, and those in the cities of Jerahmeel, and those in the cities of the Kenites,
verses.30:30: and those in Arama, and those in the cistern of Ashan, and those in Athach,
verses.30:31: and those in Hebron, and to the rest who were in those places in which David had stayed, he and his men.
verses.31:1: Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the face of the Philistines and fell dead on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:2: And the Philistines rushed upon Saul and upon his sons, and they struck down Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.
verses.31:3: And the entire weight of the battle turned against Saul, and the archers overtook him, and he was severely wounded by the archers.
verses.31:4: And Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and strike me, so that these uncircumcised men may not come and kill me, mocking me." But his armor-bearer would not, for he had been terrified with extreme terror. Therefore Saul seized the sword and fell upon it.
verses.31:5: And when his armor-bearer saw this, namely that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his own sword and died with him.
verses.31:6: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armor-bearer, and all his men together on that day.
verses.31:7: Now when the men of Israel who were across the valley and across the Jordan saw that the Israelite men had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and fled; and the Philistines came and lived there.
verses.31:8: And when the next day had come, the Philistines came to strip those who had been killed, and they found Saul and his three sons lying on Mount Gilboa.
verses.31:9: And they cut off Saul's head and stripped him of his armor, and they sent throughout the land of the Philistines all around so that it might be announced in the temple of idols and among the peoples.
verses.31:10: And they placed his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth, while they hung his body on the wall of Beth-shan.
verses.31:11: Now when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard this, all that the Philistines had done to Saul,
verses.31:12: all the bravest men rose up and walked all night, and took the corpse of Saul and the corpses of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan; and they came to Jabesh-gilead and burned them there.
verses.31:13: And they took their bones and buried them in the grove of Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days.

notes.1:5: The Vulgate reads 'partem unam tristis' ("one portion sorrowfully"), interpreting the difficult Hebrew 'appayim' as Elkanah's sorrowful countenance rather than "a double portion."
notes.1:16: The Vulgate preserves the Hebrew transliteration 'Belial' (meaning "worthlessness" or "wickedness") as a name both here and in 2:12.
notes.1:18: The Vulgate reads 'vultusque illius non sunt amplius in diversa mutati' ("her countenance was no longer changed in different ways"), expanding the concise Hebrew idiom meaning her face was no longer downcast.
notes.1:24: The Vulgate has 'tribus modiis' ("three measures"), reflecting Jerome's reckoning of one Hebrew ephah as three modii (seahs), and retains 'vitulis tribus' ("three calves") rather than the Septuagint's "a three-year-old bull."
notes.1:28: The Vulgate reads 'quibus fuerit commodatus Domino' ("that he is lent to the Lord") rather than the Hebrew "as long as he lives," uses plural 'adoraverunt' ("they worshiped") with the Septuagint, and places "And Hannah prayed and said:" at the end of 1:28 rather than at 2:1.
notes.2:3: The Vulgate reads 'vetera' ("old things", connecting Hebrew 'ataq' with the root "ancient" rather than "arrogant") and 'ipsi præparantur cogitationes' ("for Him thoughts are prepared"), where the Hebrew has "by Him actions are weighed."
notes.2:5: The Vulgate renders 'plurimos' ("very many") where the Hebrew specifies "seven," and 'saturati sunt' ("have been satisfied") where the Hebrew reads "have ceased [to hunger]."
notes.2:10: Latin 'christi sui' (like 'christo meo' in 2:35) translates Hebrew 'mashiach' ("anointed one"), a title also read messianically in Christian tradition; the Vulgate also reads 'imperium' ("dominion") where the Hebrew has "strength."
notes.2:32: The Vulgate reads 'æmulum tuum in templo' ("your rival in the temple"), understanding Hebrew 'tsar ma'on' as a rival in the sanctuary rather than "distress in the dwelling."
notes.2:36: The Vulgate reads 'ut oretur pro eo, et offerat nummum argenteum, et tortam panis' ("so that prayer may be made for him, and will offer a silver coin and a loaf of bread"), whereas the Hebrew depicts Eli's descendant bowing down to beg for silver and bread.
notes.3:1: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew terms for "rare" and "widespread" as "pretiosus" ("precious," i.e., rare and valued) and "manifesta" ("clear" or "open").
notes.3:10: The Vulgate reads "sicut vocaverat secundo" ("just as He had called the second time"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "as at the other times."
notes.3:13: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of Eli's sons cursing themselves (or God, in the Septuagint) and Eli not restraining them, the Vulgate reads "indigne agere" ("acting unworthily") and "non corripuerit" ("did not rebuke").
notes.3:21: In the Vulgate and Septuagint, "And the word of Samuel came to all Israel" concludes chapter 3, whereas in the Hebrew Masoretic Text it opens 4:1.
notes.4:1: The Vulgate (with the Septuagint) opens the chapter with the Philistines assembling for combat, a clause absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text; it also translates the place name Ebenezer literally as "lapis Adjutorii" ("the Stone of Help," as again in 5:1).
notes.4:8: The Vulgate reads "tanta exultatio" ("such great exultation"), referring back to Israel's shout in 4:5, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "nothing like this has happened before."
notes.4:18: The Vulgate describes Eli as "grandaevus" ("advanced in age"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text describes him as "heavy."
notes.4:21: The Clementine Vulgate prints "vocabit," a well-known orthographic b/v variant for "vocavit" ("she called"), translated here in the past tense in keeping with the narrative context and "ait" ("she said") in 4:22.
notes.5:5: In the Vulgate, the opening clause about Dagon's trunk begins verse 5 and adds "in loco suo" ("in its place"), whereas in the Hebrew Masoretic Text it concludes verse 4 ("only Dagon was left to him").
notes.5:6: Jerome renders the affliction euphemistically as "in the more hidden part of the buttocks" (again in 5:12); the second sentence describing the swarming villages, mice, and confusion of great death is a Vulgate and Septuagint expansion absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.5:8: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate makes the Gittites (the inhabitants of Gath) the speakers who propose carrying the ark around, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text states that the Philistines decided to move the ark to Gath.
notes.5:9: The Vulgate vividly describes the plague as causing their protruding lower bowels ("extales") to rot, and concludes with a Vulgate and Septuagint addition in which the Gittites take counsel and make leather seats for themselves.
notes.6:5: Vulgate anos aureos literally means "golden anuses" (matching the Septuagint hedras, "seats/posteriors"), depicting the afflicted bodily part as a votive offering, whereas Hebrew is commonly rendered "tumors" or "hemorrhoids." Latin satrapis ("satraps") also uses a Persian-Greek imperial title for the Philistine rulers.
notes.6:6: Vulgate postquam percussus est, tunc dimisit eos ("after he was struck, did he not then let them go") uses singular verbs referring to Pharaoh, whereas the Hebrew reads "when He dealt severely with them, did they not send them away."
notes.6:18: Vulgate Abelmagnum ("Great Abel") preserves Hebrew Abel haggedolah as a proper name rather than the variant reading "great stone," and reads usque in illum diem ("until that day") instead of "to this day." The feminine relative quae agrees grammatically with arcam ("the ark"), though the corresponding Hebrew clause refers to the landmark in Joshua's field.
notes.6:19: Vulgate reads septuaginta viros, et quinquaginta millia plebis ("seventy men and fifty thousand of the common people"), inserting "and" and distinguishing viros from plebis at a well-known numerical crux in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:1: Vulgate in Gabaa ("in Gibeah") takes Hebrew baggibah as a proper place name rather than the common noun "on the hill."
notes.7:2: Vulgate requievit ("rested") derives the underlying Hebrew verb from nuah ("to rest") rather than nahah ("to lament/mourn"), producing a distinctly Vulgate reading.
notes.7:12: Vulgate translates the Hebrew name Ebenezer directly into Latin as Lapis adjutorii ("Stone of Help") and explicitly specifies nomen loci illius ("the name of that place") rather than the stone itself.
notes.7:14: Vulgate attaches et terminos suos ("and their borders") to the restored cities and begins a new clause with liberavitque ("and He delivered"), treating Israel as the object delivered from the Philistines rather than the subject rescuing its territory as in the Hebrew.
notes.8:9: Latin jus regis ("the right of the king," repeated in 8:11) denotes the legal prerogative or custom a monarch will claim, rendering Hebrew mishpat hammelek.
notes.8:12: Vulgate tribunos, et centuriones ("tribunes and centurions") casts the military ranks in Roman terminology, substituting centurions (commanders of hundreds) where the Hebrew has commanders of fifties.
notes.8:15: Vulgate translates Hebrew sarisim literally as eunuchis ("eunuchs") rather than the broader sense "court officials."
notes.8:18: The closing clause quia petistis vobis regem ("because you have asked a king for yourselves") is a Vulgate-distinct addition not found in the Masoretic Hebrew text.
notes.9:1: Latin "filii viri Jemini" renders the Hebrew gentilic "Yemini" (Benjaminite) as the proper name Jemini alongside Benjamin (also in 9:4, 21). "Mighty in strength" literally translates Latin "fortis robore", rendering the Hebrew idiom for a man of standing or valor.
notes.9:2: Latin "electus et bonus" ("choice and good") renders the Hebrew phrase usually translated "a handsome young man", taking the Hebrew participle in its literal sense of "chosen" or "choice".
notes.9:8: Latin uses "stater" (a Greek silver coin equivalent to a shekel) to render Hebrew "shekel".
notes.9:24: Latin reads "armum" ("the shoulder") where Hebrew has "the thigh" (and omits "and what was on it"), and renders the following clause directly as "when I invited the people".
notes.9:25: The closing clause "and Saul spread a bed on the rooftop and slept" is present in the Clementine Vulgate (with a parallel in the Septuagint), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text ends the verse after they spoke on the roof.
notes.10:1: The Vulgate (agreeing with the Septuagint and 4QSam-a) includes the longer clause "and you will deliver His people... that God has anointed you as prince", which is absent from the shorter Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.10:2: Latin reads "in meridie" ("in the south", or possibly "at midday"), interpreting the Hebrew place name "Zelzah".
notes.10:8: Latin uses second-person singular verbs ("offeras... immoles", "you may offer... sacrifice", addressed to Saul), whereas Hebrew uses infinitives usually understood of Samuel.
notes.10:22: Latin reads "domi" ("at home"), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "among the baggage".
notes.10:27: "Sons of Belial" literally translates Latin "filii Belial", a biblical Hebrew idiom meaning "worthless men".
notes.11:1: The opening phrase "about a month later" (Latin "quasi post mensem", shared with the Septuagint and 4QSam-a) does not appear in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which instead reads the related consonants at the end of 10:27 as "like one keeping silent" (also reflected in Vulgate 10:27).
notes.11:6: Latin reads "spiritus Domini" ("the Spirit of the Lord", as also in 10:10), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Spirit of God".
notes.11:10: Latin reads "Mane" ("In the morning"), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Tomorrow".
notes.12:3: The Vulgate reads 'et contemnam illud hodie' ('and I will despise it today'), differing from the Hebrew ('to blind my eyes with it') and the Septuagint ('even a sandal'); 'munus' ('gift') carries the judicial sense of a bribe.
notes.12:7: The Vulgate reads 'misericordiis' ('mercies'), whereas the Hebrew text has 'righteous deeds.'
notes.12:11: The Vulgate 'Badan' ('Bedan') follows the Hebrew Masoretic Text; this deliverer is otherwise unknown by that name, while the Septuagint and Syriac read 'Barak.'
notes.12:17: Latin 'voces et pluvias' literally means 'voices and rains,' a Hebraic idiom for peals of thunder and rainstorms (likewise in 12:18).
notes.12:22: The Vulgate reads 'juravit' ('has sworn'), whereas the Hebrew has 'was pleased' or 'resolved.'
notes.13:3: The Vulgate uses 'Gabaa' consistently throughout this chapter (13:2, 3, 15, 16), whereas the Hebrew text alternates between Gibeah (13:2, 15) and Geba (13:3, 16).
notes.13:4: The Vulgate reads 'erexit se Israel adversus Philisthiim' ('Israel has risen up against the Philistines') and active 'Clamavit' ('cried out'), whereas the Hebrew has 'Israel had become odious to the Philistines' and 'the people were called out.'
notes.13:15: The middle sentence ('And the rest of the people went up after Saul... on the hill of Benjamin') is a distinctly Vulgate reading shared with the Septuagint tradition but absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:21: The Vulgate 'Retusae itaque erant acies' ('And so the edges ... were blunted') reflects an ancient interpretation of an obscure Hebrew phrase that modern scholarship identifies as a sharpening fee of one pim (about two-thirds of a shekel).
notes.13:23: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew noun phrase 'to the pass of Michmash' as a purpose clause, 'ut transcenderet in Machmas' ('to cross over into Michmash').
notes.14:15: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew term for "trembling" or "panic" twice as miraculum ("miracle"), emphasizing the sudden turmoil in the Philistine camp as a miraculous intervention from God.
notes.14:22: The closing sentence ("And there were with Saul about ten thousand men") is a Vulgate reading shared with the Septuagint that does not appear in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.14:24: The Vulgate reads sociati sunt sibi ("were joined together"), reflecting a different vocalization or reading of the Hebrew verb that the Masoretic Text renders "were hard-pressed."
notes.14:38: Latin angulos ("corners") literally reproduces the Hebrew idiom for the chiefs or leaders of the people, viewed as their cornerstones.
notes.14:41: Following the longer text also attested in the Septuagint (against the shorter Masoretic Text), the Vulgate includes Saul's full appeal and renders the sacred lots Urim and Thummim as ostensionem ("manifestation") and sanctitatem ("holiness").
notes.15:4: Vulgate renders the Hebrew place name Telaim (ba-Telaim) etymologically as "like lambs" (quasi agnos).
notes.15:9: Vulgate reads "garments" (vestibus) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has a term usually rendered "fatlings" or "secondlings" (ha-mishnim).
notes.15:12: Vulgate renders Hebrew yad ("monument") as "a triumphal arch" (fornicem triumphalem) and includes the closing clause describing Saul offering a burnt offering from the first of the spoils, which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.15:29: Vulgate reads "the Victor [lit. Triumpher] in Israel will not spare" (triumphator in Israël non parcet), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text is usually rendered "the Glory of Israel will not lie."
notes.15:32: Vulgate describes Agag as "very fat and trembling" (pinguissimus et tremens) and casts his speech as a question, "Does bitter death separate like this?" (Siccine separat amara mors?), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly rendered "Surely the bitterness of death has passed."
notes.16:4: Vulgate reads "were astonished" (admirati sunt) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "came trembling."
notes.16:6: Vulgate casts Samuel's exclamation as a question ("Is His anointed before the Lord?", Num...?) rather than the affirmative "Surely" of the Hebrew Masoretic Text; "anointed" renders Latin christus.
notes.16:13: Vulgate reads "was directed upon David" (directus est... in David), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text expresses the Spirit rushing mightily upon him.
notes.16:23: Vulgate specifies "the evil spirit from [lit. of] the Lord" (spiritus Domini malus; similarly in 16:16), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads simply "the spirit of God."
notes.17:1: Vulgate "in the borders of Dommim" (in finibus Dommim) translates the first element of the Hebrew place name Ephes-dammim as "in the borders of" and retains Dommim as the proper name. Similarly, in 17:2 Vulgate renders the Hebrew Valley of Elah literally as "the Valley of the Terebinth" (Vallem terebinthi).
notes.17:4: Vulgate vir spurius ("an illegitimate man") reflects Jerome's interpretation of the Hebrew phrase ish ha-benayim ("man of the between-space," commonly translated "champion") as denoting mixed or illegitimate birth. Vulgate also gives his height as six cubits and a palm (palmi, corresponding to Hebrew "span").
notes.17:6: Vulgate renders Hebrew kidon ("javelin" or "scimitar") as clypeus ("shield") here and in 17:45.
notes.17:35: Vulgate includes "and strangle" (et suffocabam), a detail not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text; in 17:34 Vulgate also specifies "a ram" (arietem) where the Hebrew has a general term for a sheep or lamb, and in 17:36 includes "Now I will go and take away the disgrace of the people," matching the Septuagint.
notes.17:47: Vulgate uses ecclesia ("assembly") for the gathered Israelites, and in 17:52 translates the Hebrew place name Gai as "into the valley" (in vallem).
notes.18:6: Vulgate reads "tambourines of joy" (tympanis lætitiæ) with a genitive modifier and renders the Hebrew musical instruments (shalishim) as sistris ("sistrums," metallic rattle instruments).
notes.18:9: Literally "not with straight eyes" (non rectis oculis), a Latin idiom expressing suspicion, hostility, or looking askance.
notes.18:13: Vulgate uses the Roman military title tribunum ("tribune") for a commander over a thousand men.
notes.18:21: Vulgate "In two things" (In duabus rebus) literally renders the Hebrew expression often understood as "a second time" (referring to a second offer of Saul's daughters). In 18:27 Vulgate likewise begins with "And after a few days" (Et post paucos dies), where the Hebrew closes 18:26 with "before the time had expired."
notes.19:10: Latin casso vulnere ("with a fruitless blow") is a distinctive Vulgate addition describing the spear missing David and striking the wall.
notes.19:20: The Vulgate reads spiritus Domini ("the Spirit of the Lord") here and in 19:23, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "the Spirit of God"; Jerome also varies the terms for Saul's men across the chapter (satellites, apparitores, nuntios, lictores).
notes.19:21: The closing phrase Et iratus iracundia Saul ("And Saul, enraged with anger") agrees with the Septuagint and is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.19:22: The Vulgate reads the place name Socho ("Socoh"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Secu."
notes.20:3: In the Clementine Vulgate, Davidi is dative ("And he swore again to David"), making Jonathan the subject of the oath and shifting to David with Et ille ("And the other"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has David swearing again.
notes.20:5: Throughout chapter 20 (vv. 5, 18, 24, 27, 34), the Vulgate renders the monthly New Moon observance with the Latin term calendae (the Calends, the first day of the month).
notes.20:15: The Vulgate subjunctive clause auferat Jonathan de domo sua, et requirat Dominus ("may He remove Jonathan from his house, and may the Lord require it") treats Jonathan as the direct object of the Lord's action, diverging in syntax and verse division from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.20:19: The Vulgate renders the workday reference explicitly as in die qua operari licet ("on the day when it is lawful to work").
notes.20:30: The Vulgate renders Saul's insult as Fili mulieris virum ultro rapientis ("Son of a woman who of her own accord seizes a man") and ignominiosae matris tuae ("of your disgraceful mother"), differing from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("son of a perverse, rebellious woman ... shame of your mother's nakedness").
notes.21:1: The Vulgate numbers this verse 20:43 (20:42b in many English Bibles) and the remaining verses of chapter 21 one lower than here.
notes.21:6: The Vulgate renders this difficult clause distinctly as "this journey is defiled, yet even it will be sanctified today in the vessels," whereas many Hebrew-based translations read "even on an ordinary journey, how much more today will their vessels be holy."
notes.21:8: The Vulgate reads "inside the tabernacle of the Lord" (intus in tabernaculo Domini), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "detained before the Lord."
notes.21:10: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Elah literally as "the Valley of the Terebinth" (Valle terebinthi).
notes.21:14: The Vulgate reads "kept collapsing between their hands" (collabebatur inter manus eorum) and "kept striking against the doors of the gate" (impingebat in ostia portae), whereas the Hebrew describes David acting madly in their hands and making marks on the doors.
notes.22:6: The Vulgate reads "in the grove that is in Ramah" (in nemore quod est in Rama), treating Rama as a proper place name, whereas the Hebrew refers to a tamarisk tree "on the height" in Gibeah.
notes.22:7: "sons of Jemini" renders the Vulgate filii Jemini literally, reflecting the shorter Hebrew gentilic form for Benjaminites; "tribunes and centurions" preserves the Vulgate's Roman military titles for commanders of thousands and hundreds.
notes.22:14: The Vulgate reads "going at your command" (pergens ad imperium tuum), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text is commonly rendered "captain of your bodyguard."
notes.22:19: "with the edge of the sword" translates the Latin idiom in ore gladii (literally "in the mouth of the sword"), mirroring the corresponding Hebrew expression.
notes.22:22: The Vulgate reads "of all the souls of your father" (omnium animarum patris tui), without the word "house" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:14: The Vulgate adds "on a shaded mountain" (in monte opaco), a descriptive phrase not present in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:15: Here and in verses 16, 18, and 19, the Vulgate translates Hebrew horeshah as the common noun "forest" (silva) rather than as the proper place name "Horesh."
notes.23:22: The Vulgate reads "for he thinks about me that I craftily lie in wait for him" (recogitat enim de me, quod callide insidier ei), making David the subject of the reflection, whereas the Hebrew reads "for it is told to me that he is very cunning."
notes.23:26: The Vulgate renders David's reaction as "despairing of being able to escape" (desperabat se posse evadere), whereas the Hebrew describes David hurrying to get away.
notes.23:28: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew place name Sela-hammahlekoth as "the Dividing Rock" (Petram dividentem).
notes.24:3: Latin "etiam super abruptissimas petras, quae solis ibicibus perviae sunt" renders the Hebrew place name ("Rocks of the Wild Goats") descriptively as steep crags passable only to wild goats (ibexes).
notes.24:4: Latin "ut purgaret ventrem" ("to relieve his bowels") explicitly renders the Hebrew euphemism "to cover his feet."
